site.name: RepoTunnel
site.tagline: Controlled local access for AI development work.
site.description: Connect ChatGPT Web to local projects with RepoTunnel. Read and edit files, run commands and review work with unlimited Direct HTTPS connection usage.

products.title: Local projects and files
products.description: RepoTunnel gives AI access to only the local projects you explicitly approve, with separate read-only/read-write and AI Review/AI Auto controls.

sections.title: Why the project boundary matters
paragraphs: AI is most useful when it can work with the real repository, but a broad host filesystem is the wrong security boundary. RepoTunnel registers explicit workspace roots and exposes those roots to AI by opaque workspace IDs rather than arbitrary absolute paths.
bullets: Canonical project root stored locally by RepoTunnel
Absolute paths and parent traversal rejected
Common credential and private-key files protected

sections.title: Read-only and read/write are separate from review policy
paragraphs: A workspace can be read-only or read/write. For writable projects, AI Review queues supported changes for local approval, while AI Auto can apply compatible operations immediately without removing the underlying security boundaries.
bullets: AI Auto removes repeated approval prompts for supported operations

sections.title: Large repositories
paragraphs: RepoTunnel includes paged project inspection, paged directory listing, large-file range reads, and incremental search cursors so large codebases do not need to be transmitted or scanned in one giant operation.

sections.title: Projects is the place to begin
paragraphs: Open an existing folder or clone a supported repository, then select that approved workspace in the Projects rail. The app shows its access, AI-change policy, command policy and current health.
The project setup panel reports the detected framework, package manager, dependencies and development command. Use Prepare project only when setup is needed and the proposed work is appropriate.

links.label: Add and prepare your first project

sections.title: Work with files and context
paragraphs: The workspace editor opens files from the selected project, supports project/file search and preserves editing context across normal sessions. Project overview helps identify the repository before making changes.
Project Memory stores useful goals, decisions, preferences and intended next steps beside factual continuity state.

products.title: MCP gateway
products.description: RepoTunnel exposes capability-oriented MCP tools through an authenticated boundary while keeping the raw gateway on loopback.

sections.title: Local-first transport
paragraphs: The raw MCP service binds to loopback. Remote clients reach it through a supported authenticated connection path instead of turning the local workspace gateway into a public host listener.

sections.title: Capability-oriented tools
paragraphs: RepoTunnel does not expose an unrestricted host API. File, Git, command, browser, desktop, phone, team, continuity, and video operations each retain their own validation and permission rules.
bullets: Workspace IDs instead of absolute roots
Remote MCP cannot self-approve local Review actions

sections.title: OAuth
paragraphs: Public MCP access uses RepoTunnel's OAuth boundary where applicable, including dynamic-client registration and PKCE-compatible flows. Authorization state lives outside project repositories and can be revoked without deleting approved projects.

sections.title: Verify the complete route
paragraphs: Start the local gateway, choose a supported connection path and authorize the intended AI client. Then list approved projects and request a bounded read of a non-sensitive file.
This validates transport, authentication, tool discovery and workspace access together. Repeat discovery after a schema change when the client caches the available tools.

links.label: Connect and verify an AI client

products.title: Terminal and managed processes
products.description: RepoTunnel separates disposable verification commands from live project terminal/process work and refuses to silently fall back to unrestricted host execution.

sections.title: Two execution models
paragraphs: Verification presets run in disposable project copies with network disabled. Live terminal commands and managed processes operate on the approved workspace through the platform's AI sandbox.

sections.title: Managed processes
paragraphs: Long-running builds, dev servers, and workers get durable RepoTunnel IDs, bounded output, stop/restart support, and process-state tracking. Linux supports validated process reattachment across a complete RepoTunnel restart; Windows and macOS do not claim that capability yet.

sections.title: Use the Commands screen
paragraphs: Select the intended project in Commands. The screen combines a live one-shot terminal, persistent processes, application launches, managed browser automation and monitoring.
Use a one-shot command for finite work, a managed process for a development server or worker, and a discovered disposable preset for isolated verification.

sections.title: Follow a real development task
bullets: Inspect the project’s detected commands and readiness.
Run the appropriate build/test in the disposable sandbox when persistent writes are unnecessary.
Start the preview server as a managed process when UI testing needs it.
Inspect the process output and real application state before reporting completion.
Stop or restart that specific managed process when the task requires it.

sections.title: Keep runtime recovery evidence
paragraphs: Managed processes expose identity, status and bounded incremental logs. Connection/UI reconnection is different from a full application restart; complete restart reattachment is currently advertised on Linux only.
The native sandbox must be available for AI execution. A policy denial is a reported boundary, not permission to fall back to an unrestricted host shell.

products.title: Git and GitHub
products.description: RepoTunnel supports bounded Git inspection and validated stage/commit flows while keeping push tied to a current explicit human instruction.

sections.title: Safe Git surface
paragraphs: RepoTunnel exposes a fixed Git capability surface rather than arbitrary Git arguments.
bullets: Bounded status, diff, branch and log
Secret preflight before staging and publishing
Hooks and GPG signing disabled for controlled commit execution

sections.title: Push is different
paragraphs: AI Auto is not standing permission to publish. A push is accepted only when the current human instruction explicitly authorizes publishing, and RepoTunnel performs a committed-tree secret preflight before the push.

sections.title: From a change to a local commit
paragraphs: Choose the repository in Git, inspect its branch and changed paths, and review the relevant staged or unstaged diff. Stage only the intended files before requesting a commit.
RepoTunnel validates the selected content and staged state. It does not stage unrelated changes implicitly while committing.

sections.title: Recover a tracked text file
paragraphs: Restore-to-HEAD is available for eligible unstaged, non-conflicted tracked text files. The restoration goes through the safe-editing layer and applicable review policy.
RepoTunnel avoids silently discarding staged changes. For broader saved file state, inspect History or checkpoints.

sections.title: Use the connected GitHub identity
paragraphs: Supported workflows use RepoTunnel’s trusted GitHub connection without passing its credential to the AI shell or chat. Authentication management stays local and user-controlled.
A missing token inside a sandbox is not enough to conclude that the app’s GitHub connection is broken. Check the authoritative connection state.

products.title: Browser automation
products.description: Navigate, inspect and interact with managed Chromium browsers through RepoTunnel, with protection for sensitive fields and uncertain actions.

sections.title: Browser workflow
paragraphs: RepoTunnel tracks tabs, document generations, navigation results, console/network diagnostics, downloads, uploads, DOM inspection, screenshots, and semantic accessibility snapshots.
bullets: Navigate, click, type, scroll and reload

sections.title: Handle uncertain browser actions
paragraphs: State-changing browser actions create mutation receipts. If helper transport is lost after a mutation may already have happened, RepoTunnel reports the action as ambiguous and reconnects for observation rather than automatically replaying it.

sections.title: Semantic protection
paragraphs: Short-lived semantic references are bound to the current browser state and sensitive fields cannot be typed through the semantic path.

sections.title: Use it to verify the app you built
paragraphs: Open the managed browser controls from Commands, start the selected supported browser and navigate to the local preview or approved site. Inspect the current document and capture evidence for the behavior under test.
Console/network diagnostics, screenshots, downloads and uploads support the workflow within their capability boundaries.

sections.title: Keep the page state current
paragraphs: Refresh the live document state before using a semantic reference. References belong to a particular page state, and stale references cannot be treated as permanent element IDs.
If a click or type action reports an ambiguous outcome after dispatch, inspect what happened before issuing another state-changing action.

links.label: Handle semantic actions and uncertain results

products.title: Isolated AI Workspace
products.description: AI Workspace lets supported GUI applications run in an isolated virtual desktop so AI workflows do not need to take over the user's normal desktop.

sections.title: Separate from your normal desktop
paragraphs: AI Workspace provides a shared isolated virtual desktop with per-application session ownership. Multiple AI-owned app sessions can coexist within its bounded resource model.

sections.title: Platform adapters
paragraphs: Linux uses a private AT-SPI environment for the isolated desktop. Windows UI Automation and macOS Accessibility adapters share the policy model, but native behavior should only be claimed where it has been validated on that operating system.

sections.title: Choose an isolated GUI session
paragraphs: Use AI Workspace for a task that needs supported graphical applications in a separate virtual desktop. Start a session, open the required application and inspect that session’s screen/state before interacting.
Keep the session associated with the approved project. Use browser automation for browser-specific work and workspace file tools for direct file work when those surfaces are sufficient.

sections.title: Verify the artifact after the GUI action
paragraphs: Saving through a graphical application still needs a confirmed output. Inspect the resulting file or application state, handle overwrite dialogs deliberately and check that the requested artifact was created.
Available adapters and isolation behavior differ by native platform; Linux remains the primary live-validated host.

products.title: Desktop control
products.description: RepoTunnel can control user-enabled desktop applications through a bounded app permission layer while blocking control of RepoTunnel itself.

sections.title: Permission first
paragraphs: Desktop control is disabled until the user enables the relevant project-level permission. AI actions target enabled applications and cannot use RepoTunnel's own UI as a control surface.

sections.title: When to use it
paragraphs: Use normal Desktop Control when interaction with an already-running real desktop application is genuinely required. Use AI Workspace when the AI should work without interrupting the user's real desktop.

sections.title: Ground actions in the selected application
paragraphs: Grant desktop permission locally, inspect the actual application state and use the available semantic or visual controls for the task.
Desktop permission is separate from project write access. RepoTunnel blocks AI control of RepoTunnel itself and does not silently widen a permission when an operation is denied.

sections.title: Use the narrowest suitable surface
paragraphs: A build is usually a command workflow, a repository edit is usually a file workflow, and web testing is usually a managed-browser workflow. Reserve desktop actions for work that depends on a native application’s interface.
For an isolated multi-application task, use AI Workspace and verify its saved output.

products.title: Android Phone Access
products.description: Connect a selected Android device for live screen control and approved operations, with separate permissions for phone access.

sections.title: Connection model
paragraphs: Wireless Debugging is preferred, with authorized USB fallback for the same selected device. AI-facing tools use an opaque device identity rather than raw ADB connection details.
bullets: Apps, files, APK, settings, shell/log/network operations depending on granted capabilities

sections.title: Sensitive-app behavior
paragraphs: When a payment-sensitive app is foreground, RepoTunnel blocks AI screen observation and control paths. Android permissions and device policy remain authoritative even under Full Access.

sections.title: Set up the selected Android device
paragraphs: Open Phone, authorize the device locally and choose the AI access level. Wireless Debugging is preferred; an authorized USB connection can provide fallback for the same selected phone.
AI tools cannot pair or select a device, increase access, change Limited grants or unpause Phone Access.

sections.title: Choose capabilities for the task
bullets: Live screen and local human control.
Guarded AI observation, touch, typing and navigation.
Supported app management and APK installation/removal.
Bounded device files, settings, diagnostics, logs and network checks.
Optional Phone Helper semantic references and transactions, with user-enabled Accessibility.

sections.title: Check the actual device result
paragraphs: A Full access setting still respects Android permissions and vendor/device policy. Inspect the returned result instead of assuming a setting write or application operation is supported everywhere.
The bundled Phone Helper is a narrow companion to this workflow, not a general-purpose separate RepoTunnel Android app.

links.label: Phone privacy and sensitive foreground apps

products.title: GPT Agents and Team Mode
products.description: Team Mode coordinates two persistent AI engineers with planning, distinct task ownership, path claims, cross-review and evidence-based completion.

sections.title: Coordination before parallelism
paragraphs: Both engineers join before planning begins. Each posts a plan, takes a distinct implementation task, and confirms the split before RepoTunnel unlocks parallel implementation.
bullets: One primary owner per implementation task
One active implementation task per agent

sections.title: Persistent team
paragraphs: Completing one work request does not end the team. The team remains attached to the project until the user explicitly ends it in the desktop app.

sections.title: Start from GPT Agents
paragraphs: Select the approved project in GPT Agents, enter a product goal and concrete success criteria, and create the Team. The app supplies separate Engineer A and B kickoff prompts for their external AI chats.
Both engineers join before the planning/split barrier unlocks implementation. The desktop screen shows their workflow stage, current tasks and verification evidence.

sections.title: Continue without recreating the team
paragraphs: A completed work request returns the persistent Team to Ready. Give the next request to an attached AI chat so it can register the new work cycle in the same Team.
Pause blocks Team work temporarily; End Team is the user-owned action that permanently detaches the two identities. MCP cannot force an arbitrary completely idle web chat to begin generating.

products.title: Continuity and recovery
products.description: Resume interrupted work with live Git, process and activity state alongside project context, so older notes can be checked against the current project.

sections.title: What Resume v2 uses
paragraphs: RepoTunnel distinguishes factual live state from saved intent. Git status, recent activity, managed-process state and current project evidence take precedence over stale memory.

sections.title: ChatGPT continuation companion
paragraphs: The optional Chromium continuation extension binds only exact ChatGPT conversations that the user explicitly saves. It waits for an idle completed response and empty composer, prepares the exact checkpoint, authorizes one send, and does not blindly replay an uncertain post-send outcome.

sections.title: Keep intentions and facts together
paragraphs: Project Memory preserves the goals and decisions another chat needs. Live continuity records what actually completed, what is active or blocked and what the current runtime/Git state shows.
Resume by inspecting that state first. An older plan or a waiting request is not evidence that a file was changed or a process started.

sections.title: Recover files and resume the conversation
paragraphs: History and checkpoints provide their documented local file recovery scope. The optional Chromium continuation companion targets exact saved ChatGPT chats and waits for safe delivery conditions.
The companion’s source installation is separate from the desktop release assets. Use its setup and privacy guide before pairing it.

products.title: Video tools
products.description: RepoTunnel can analyze supported media and maintain durable video-production projects with script, scenes, narration, subtitles, rendering and QA state.

sections.title: Video Intelligence
paragraphs: Background jobs can prepare transcript, visual, instruction-oriented or full analysis from supported public URLs or approved local media. Existing captions are preferred; bounded smart frames and compact audio are used when needed.

sections.title: Video Production
paragraphs: Video Projects persist script/storyboard/timeline state, generated scenes, narration, subtitles, previews/renders, QA evidence and asset-license provenance.
bullets: Deterministic HTML/CSS/GSAP tutorial scenes where appropriate
Optional installed creative engines for suitable story workflows
Preview and QA gates before final render

sections.title: Choose Analyze or Projects
paragraphs: Analyze is the Video Intelligence view for supported public/local media. Choose Full, Transcript focus, Visual focus or Tutorial focus and, when useful, a targeted time range.
Projects is the production view for durable Video Projects. It keeps script/storyboard, scene and asset state with timeline, rendering, preview and QA work.

sections.title: Build a reviewable production pipeline
paragraphs: Plan the script and scenes, retain source/license records for assets, generate or import the required material, and inspect draft previews before a final render.
Tutorial scenes can use deterministic HTML/CSS/GSAP capture. Suitable story shots can use native motion or optional installed creative engines; large tooling is not silently installed.

sections.title: Keep evidence and publication separate
paragraphs: A video analysis is evidence about the media. Instructions found inside it do not authorize execution, installs or edits.
A finished render still needs QA and an explicit instruction before external publication or upload. Real software demonstrations should reflect actual observed behavior.

products.title: Unlimited Direct HTTPS connections
products.description: Connect ChatGPT to local projects with Direct HTTPS. RepoTunnel adds no monthly tunnel request quota; you manage the endpoint, routing and trusted TLS.

sections.title: No monthly tunnel request quota
paragraphs: Direct HTTPS connects an AI client to your own running RepoTunnel HTTPS endpoint. It provides unlimited connection usage without RepoTunnel adding a monthly tunnel request quota or connection-credit allowance.
Keep the service and HTTPS endpoint running to use the connection for successive project tasks, fixes, reviews and improvements. Workspace permissions and OAuth stay in force.

links.label: Work on local projects from ChatGPT Web

sections.title: Verified Linux path
paragraphs: The documented Linux Mint setup uses Route64 + WireGuard for a public IPv6 path, DuckDNS for a stable hostname, Let's Encrypt for TLS, and an IPv4-to-IPv6 frontend when required by IPv4-only clients.
bullets: Public TCP 443 → RepoTunnel Direct HTTPS listener

sections.title: Who should use it
paragraphs: Use Direct HTTPS when you want to manage your own public connection and work without a tunnel provider’s monthly request allowance. It requires control of the network route, hostname and certificate lifecycle.
The documented path is validated on Linux. A managed provider such as ngrok offers a simpler setup when you prefer a hosted relay.

sections.title: Follow HTTPS Setup in the app
paragraphs: The guided screen checks local requirements, Internet connectivity, the selected hostname/DNS and the final Direct HTTPS endpoint. Complete each stage using its reported evidence.
The current verified topology is Linux-specific and requires a reachable public network path and trusted TLS. Keep the raw MCP gateway bound to loopback.

links.label: Direct HTTPS setup with screenshots and checks

sections.title: Keep the connection available
paragraphs: Keep RepoTunnel and its HTTPS listener running on a computer that stays connected to the internet. After a reboot or network change, check the public route and trusted HTTPS response before continuing.
Maintain DNS records and certificate renewal for the hostname your AI client uses. Use the connection diagnostics to investigate a failed health check or OAuth discovery response.

products.title: Local model chat
products.description: Ask a local model about your selected project, control the included context and opt into safe edit proposals from RepoTunnel’s Home screen.

sections.title: A conversation inside the desktop app
paragraphs: Home can use a model already exposed by Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp on a local loopback endpoint. The app lists reachable models rather than silently selecting a cloud fallback.

sections.title: Context stays tied to the selected project
paragraphs: Ask about the approved project and include a current file, selected code or an existing diagnostic when relevant. Bounded context and returned sources help you understand what informed the response.

sections.title: Edit proposals are an explicit choice
paragraphs: Allow edits opts the next message into the safe project-edit path and resets after sending. Inspect the resulting History state and verify the file outcome rather than assuming model text changed the project.

sections.title: Set up the right AI path
paragraphs: Start the local runtime and choose an available model for Home. Configure Connect separately when you want an external MCP client such as ChatGPT to work with the project.

products.title: Activity history and recovery
products.description: Inspect recorded AI work, review pending changes and use saved versions or checkpoints to recover the accessible files of an approved project.

sections.title: See what actually happened
paragraphs: History connects recorded file, command, process, browser, Git and Team activity with their outcomes. Search and filter the selected project to find the relevant request.

sections.title: Review before applying
paragraphs: AI Review keeps pending changes local for inspection and approval. Current-file validation prevents a prepared text request from silently overwriting intervening edits.

sections.title: Return to a known file state
paragraphs: Saved versions and checkpoints provide distinct recovery controls. Review the target and affected paths, confirm restoration locally and verify the resulting project files.

sections.title: Retain useful recovery points
paragraphs: Name and manage checkpoints before large changes, and choose retention settings deliberately. Clearing saved history or snapshots does not edit current files but removes those recovery options.

products.title: Workflow readiness
products.description: Check whether an approved project supports inspection, safe editing, sandbox verification and Git before beginning an AI development task.

sections.title: Inspect before starting the work
paragraphs: Checks reads the selected project’s readiness without creating test files, executing project code or staging a commit. It helps you identify the setup step that the intended task needs.

sections.title: Act on the reported state
paragraphs: Ready, Limited and Blocked describe capability availability. A detailed item and recommended next step are more useful than treating every Limited result as a broken project.

sections.title: Respect intentional limits
paragraphs: A read-only project can be suitable for analysis even when editing is unavailable. Enable only the capability required for the current task and rerun readiness after relevant setup changes.

sections.title: Use actual verification for the result
paragraphs: After preflight, run the appropriate build/test in Commands, inspect the recorded result and review the intended Git changes. A readiness badge and a successful test provide different evidence.

products.title: ChatGPT continuation companion
products.description: Use the optional Chromium extension to deliver authorized continuation checkpoints to exact saved ChatGPT chats when they are safely idle.

sections.title: Keep the intended conversation attached
paragraphs: Explicitly save up to five exact ChatGPT conversation URLs. The companion targets those saved chats rather than guessing a conversation to continue.

sections.title: Wait for safe delivery conditions
paragraphs: The companion waits for a completed idle response, an empty composer and no recent human typing. RepoTunnel authorizes a checkpoint before one send attempt; uncertain outcomes are not automatically repeated.

sections.title: Install the source companion
paragraphs: Load extensions/chatgpt-continuation from RepoTunnel’s main branch using a compatible Chromium browser’s Load unpacked control. The published v0.4.1 desktop release does not provide a separate extension asset.

sections.title: Understand its narrow data scope
paragraphs: The documented companion stores saved conversation identifiers and bounded connection status locally. It communicates with the saved ChatGPT page and the dedicated loopback bridge, with no analytics or third-party tracking.

solutions.title: Work on local projects from ChatGPT Web
solutions.description: Connect ChatGPT Web to your local projects with RepoTunnel. Read and edit files, run commands and review work through a Direct HTTPS connection.

sections.title: Connect ChatGPT to your local projects
paragraphs: RepoTunnel lets you work on your local projects directly from a regular ChatGPT Web conversation. With the Direct HTTPS setup, ChatGPT connects to RepoTunnel running on your computer.
Use GPT‑6 Sol or GPT‑5.6 Sol, where available in ChatGPT, to read and edit files, run commands, investigate problems and manage the projects you have approved for access.

sections.title: Work with the actual project
paragraphs: Instead of copying files into chat and manually applying every suggested change, ask ChatGPT to work with the actual project. For example, ask it to inspect your website, understand the code, fix an issue, run the relevant checks and explain the results.
RepoTunnel carries out authorized actions in your local environment and returns the results to the conversation. You can review what changed, discuss the results and continue working from there.

sections.title: Unlimited Direct HTTPS connection usage
paragraphs: Direct HTTPS provides unlimited connection usage without RepoTunnel adding a monthly tunnel request quota or connection-credit allowance. Your ongoing project work does not depend on a tunnel provider’s monthly request allowance.
Keep RepoTunnel and your HTTPS endpoint running, and use that connection for successive tasks, fixes, reviews and improvements.

sections.title: Use your existing ChatGPT conversation
paragraphs: This workflow uses your existing ChatGPT Web conversation. You do not need a separate OpenAI API key or API token purchases for those chats, and you do not need to open ChatGPT Work or Codex to work on your local projects.
Give instructions in ChatGPT, let RepoTunnel perform the approved local actions and review the results in the same conversation.

sections.title: Keep access under your control
paragraphs: Choose the project folders ChatGPT can access and the policy each workspace uses. Read-only access is available for inspection, while AI Review lets you approve proposed changes and supported AI Auto actions follow the selected workspace policy.
Filesystem, command, Git and publishing rules remain enforced throughout the connection.

sections.title: Get connected
paragraphs: Start with one approved project. The documented Direct HTTPS setup is validated on Linux and needs a reachable public network path, a stable hostname and trusted TLS. The setup guide includes provider links, screenshots and checks for each stage.
bullets: Install RepoTunnel and add the project you want to work on
Choose read-only or read-write access and AI Review or AI Auto
Complete Direct HTTPS setup and its reachability checks
Add the exact MCP endpoint in ChatGPT and complete OAuth
Verify with list_workspaces and a permitted project read
Ask ChatGPT to inspect, change or check the approved project

solutions.title: Access local files with defined permissions
solutions.description: Use an explicit workspace boundary, protected-path rules and review controls instead of arbitrary host filesystem access.

sections.title: Least privilege by project
paragraphs: RepoTunnel uses workspace IDs and relative paths. Absolute paths, parent traversal and symlink escapes are rejected before file operations reach the filesystem.

sections.title: Why this differs from a raw shell
paragraphs: A raw shell starts from broad host authority. RepoTunnel instead exposes bounded capabilities whose inputs are validated against the approved workspace and current policy.

solutions.title: Connect an AI client to development tools
solutions.description: Use RepoTunnel as the authenticated bridge between an MCP-compatible AI client and approved projects, terminal, Git, browser, desktop and device capabilities.

sections.title: One gateway, multiple capability boundaries
paragraphs: MCP is the transport and tool contract. RepoTunnel's Rust backend remains the policy boundary for the actual local resources behind those tools.

sections.title: Remote without public raw access
paragraphs: The raw MCP gateway stays on loopback. Supported remote connection providers forward authenticated traffic through RepoTunnel's public boundary.

solutions.title: Test web apps with AI browser automation
solutions.description: Connect code changes to managed browser verification with navigation receipts, DOM inspection, screenshots and diagnostics.

sections.title: Close the build-test-browser loop
paragraphs: After changing a web project, an AI can start the dev server, open it in RepoTunnel's managed browser, inspect the rendered page, interact with controls, and review console/network failures without switching to an unrestricted desktop browser automation path.

sections.title: Mutation safety
paragraphs: Clicks and typed actions produce receipts. If transport fails after dispatch, RepoTunnel treats the result as ambiguous and requires observation before another mutation instead of assuming the action failed.

solutions.title: Use AI with sandboxed terminal commands
solutions.description: Run builds, tests, package commands and managed processes through RepoTunnel's platform-aware execution boundaries.

sections.title: Verification and live work are different
paragraphs: Disposable verification presets run in isolated project copies with networking disabled, while real workspace terminal/process work uses the fail-closed platform sandbox.
bullets: No unrestricted fallback if the sandbox is unavailable

solutions.title: Use ChatGPT with Git safely
solutions.description: Inspect, stage and commit validated changes while preserving an explicit human boundary around publishing.

sections.title: Local autonomy
paragraphs: RepoTunnel can expose bounded Git status/diff/log and validated stage/commit operations inside an approved repository.

sections.title: Remote publication remains explicit
paragraphs: A normal push requires a current explicit human instruction. AI Auto does not convert into standing publish permission.

solutions.title: Work with an Android phone using AI
solutions.description: Connect a selected Android phone for capability-gated screen control, files, apps and diagnostics while keeping sensitive access under user control.

sections.title: User-controlled access
paragraphs: The user selects the device and chooses Off, Limited or Full capability access. MCP cannot silently pair a different phone, raise access, change grants or unpause Phone Access.

sections.title: Guard sensitive foreground apps
paragraphs: Payment-sensitive foreground applications block AI observation/control paths instead of attempting to bypass Android or app security policy.

solutions.title: Coordinate two AI engineers on one repo
solutions.description: Use Team Mode to split meaningful implementation work, protect edit ownership and require cross-review before completion.
keywords: two AI agents coding same repo

sections.title: Parallel without file races
paragraphs: RepoTunnel coordinates task ownership and path claims so the two engineers work on distinct scopes rather than racing on the same files.

sections.title: Persistent collaboration
paragraphs: The team stays attached across requests until the user explicitly ends it.

solutions.title: Recover long AI sessions after interruptions
solutions.description: Use RepoTunnel's factual activity history, Resume v2, Project Memory and managed-process state to continue without restarting from stale assumptions.

sections.title: Recover from what actually happened
paragraphs: RepoTunnel's resume snapshot is built from current Git/activity/process state plus bounded saved semantic context, so live facts override stale remembered next steps.

sections.title: Optional exact-chat continuation
paragraphs: The Chromium continuation companion can deliver a RepoTunnel-generated continuation checkpoint only to exact ChatGPT conversations the user explicitly saves.

docs.title: What is RepoTunnel
docs.description: Understand the local-first gateway model and what RepoTunnel is designed to control.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: RepoTunnel is a local-first AI workspace gateway. It connects AI clients to the projects and local tools you approve, with separate controls for reading, editing and taking actions.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard that lets AI applications connect to external tools and data. RepoTunnel acts as an MCP server on your machine: your AI client requests a tool, and RepoTunnel checks the workspace permissions before carrying it out.

sections.title: Core workflow
bullets: Choose workspace access and AI mode
Inspect and work through capability-specific tools
Verify the result from live project state

sections.title: What RepoTunnel is not
paragraphs: RepoTunnel is not a hosted coding environment, a cloud drive, a replacement AI model, or a general unrestricted remote desktop. The desktop app remains the local control plane.

sections.title: Who should use it
paragraphs: RepoTunnel is intended for people who want an MCP-compatible AI client to work with real local projects while retaining machine-side control over what is accessible. It is useful for code review, bounded editing, repository investigation, tests, browser workflows and supported device tasks.
It is not a replacement for your AI provider, your source-control system, your operating system permissions or your own review of high-impact changes.

sections.title: The minimum setup
paragraphs: Install the desktop app, approve one project folder, select a read-only or read-write permission, and start an authenticated connection that your AI client can reach.

From the AI client, ask for the registered workspaces. Then try reading a non-sensitive file inside the approved project. That simple round trip verifies both tool discovery and actual filesystem authorization.
bullets: Start read-only if you only need analysis.
Choose AI Review when you want to inspect edits before they touch files.
Enable additional device or desktop capabilities independently when needed.

sections.title: Know the limits
paragraphs: Linux is the primary live-validated development platform. Windows and macOS releases exist, but native automation coverage and complete process recovery are not identical on every operating system. Review the platform reference for the feature you intend to use.
Remote connections depend on an accessible authenticated HTTPS endpoint. RepoTunnel itself does not magically make a local-only service reachable from the public Internet.

docs.title: A guide to the RepoTunnel app
docs.description: Walk through every RepoTunnel sidebar screen, learn where each workflow lives and find practical guides for projects, teams, recovery and the extension.

sections.title: Start with one project and one task
paragraphs: The desktop app is the local control plane. The website explains what each screen does, how its workflow fits together and which capability needs a separate permission or setup step.
Start by approving the intended project. Select only the access required for the task, inspect readiness, connect your chosen AI client and verify a small read before expanding the work.

sections.title: Home
paragraphs: Use the in-app chat with a selected local model, inspect Gateway and Remote status, and open quick actions for projects, checkpoints, safety scans and Pause AI access.

sections.title: Projects
paragraphs: Add or clone a trusted folder, select it in the project rail and choose read-only/read-write access independently of AI Review/AI Auto.
The Projects page also shows framework/dependency setup, project overview and Project Memory. Selecting a file opens the workspace editor with search and editor tools.

sections.title: GPT Agents
paragraphs: GPT Agents is the app’s entry point for Team Mode. Create a persistent two-engineer team for one approved project, supply a goal and success criteria, then copy the separate Engineer A and B kickoffs into their intended AI chats.
Follow the shared planning, task ownership, path claims, cross-review and verification stages. Completing a work request keeps the team attached; End Team is a separate human choice.

sections.title: Video
paragraphs: Video has Projects and Analyze views. Analyze runs Video Intelligence on supported public or approved local media; Projects manages durable production work with scenes, assets, rendering and QA.
Choose Transcript focus, Visual focus, Tutorial focus or Full according to the evidence you need. Publication and large optional-tool downloads require their own user decisions.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: History combines pending local review, the selected project’s activity/version timeline and checkpoint management. Pending requests can belong to different approved projects, so check each request’s workspace label; checkpoints can use an all-projects view.
Use it to inspect what actually applied, failed or is still waiting. Recovery controls target their documented file scope; they do not reverse arbitrary remote side effects.

sections.title: Checks
paragraphs: Choose a project and run Check workflow to inspect end-to-end readiness. The result is Ready, Limited or Blocked and includes a recommended next step.
The readiness inspection is read-only. Actual build/test execution is available through Commands.

sections.title: Git
paragraphs: Inspect the approved repository’s branch, HEAD and staged/unstaged paths, then review diffs and stage explicit files. Commits use already-staged changes.
Remote push remains a separately authorized publishing action, including in AI Auto. Git support requires an approved root with its own .git directory.

sections.title: Connect
paragraphs: Manage the local MCP gateway, public provider and optional managed client connection. Configure ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Direct HTTPS or the optional Secure MCP Tunnel path as appropriate.
The local gateway stays on loopback. Confirm the HTTPS/authentication path and a real tool call before treating an external client as connected.

sections.title: Commands
paragraphs: Use the project selector to work with live one-shot commands, persistent managed processes, launches, browser automation and monitoring.

Choose disposable verification when a discovered build/test/check preset is sufficient. Choose a live command or managed process when the work needs persistent project changes or a long-running service.

sections.title: Phone
paragraphs: Pair and select your Android device locally, choose Off, Limited or Full AI access and manage Pause AI independently.
The Phone panel provides live screen/control and supported device capabilities. Permissions, sensitive foreground apps and Android policy remain authoritative.

sections.title: HTTPS Setup
paragraphs: This screen guides the advanced Direct HTTPS path through local requirements, Internet reachability, hostname/DNS checks and final endpoint verification.
Follow the displayed stage results. It requires a working public route and trusted TLS; a hostname alone does not make a private local gateway reachable.

sections.title: Settings
paragraphs: Review runtime diagnostics, startup preferences, signed-update state and local history retention. The current platform’s installation and automation limits still apply.

sections.title: Help
paragraphs: Use the built-in guidance for projects, AI modes, security, Git and recovery. Shortcut groups cover workspace navigation, the editor and terminal.

sections.title: Optional ChatGPT continuation extension
paragraphs: RepoTunnel Continuation is a Chromium companion that delivers authorized checkpoints to exact ChatGPT conversations you explicitly save. It is useful for eligible interrupted or long-running work, and it waits for a safe idle chat with an empty composer.
The extension source is in extensions/chatgpt-continuation on the project’s main branch. It is loaded unpacked and is not a separate desktop v0.4.1 release asset.

docs.title: Installation overview
docs.description: Choose the correct RepoTunnel package for Linux, Windows or macOS and verify the downloaded release.

sections.title: Current public release
paragraphs: The current public release documented by the project is v0.4.1 (2026-10-05). Use the official GitHub Release assets and checksum file.

sections.title: After installation
bullets: Choose the project's access mode and AI policy
Run a real RepoTunnel tool call to verify the full path

sections.title: Pick the right package
paragraphs: The current project publishes official Linux DEB/RPM/AppImage packages, Windows NSIS/MSI installers and separate macOS DMGs for Apple Silicon and Intel. Choose the package that matches both your operating system and architecture.
bullets: Linux Mint, Ubuntu or Debian on x64: .deb
macOS: Apple Silicon or Intel DMG

sections.title: Check the package before running it
paragraphs: Use the official GitHub release page and SHA-256 checksum document to confirm you are installing the intended release rather than a random third-party download.
Opening the app successfully is only the first check. Confirm its reported version matches the release, then move to the first-project guide.
sections.note: Packages for several operating systems do not imply feature-for-feature native parity. Native runtime capabilities are described in the platform status guide.

docs.title: Add your first project
docs.description: Approve a local project without exposing unrelated folders.

sections.title: Add or clone
paragraphs: Use RepoTunnel's local project picker to register an existing project, or use its GitHub workflow to clone a repository into a project location you control.

sections.title: Choose access
bullets: Read/write + AI Review: writes wait for local approval
Read/write + AI Auto: supported writes can apply automatically inside the existing security boundaries

sections.title: Verify
paragraphs: Ask the connected AI client to list approved workspaces and inspect the selected project before allowing it to edit.

sections.title: What exactly gets approved
paragraphs: A workspace is a real local folder registered by RepoTunnel. The AI uses an opaque workspace identifier instead of receiving an arbitrary host path. RepoTunnel resolves file operations within the approved root and applies protected-path and symlink rules.
Choose a normal development folder for your first run. You do not need to approve your entire home directory or an entire disk.

sections.title: Test with a non-destructive request
paragraphs: After connecting your MCP client, ask it to list approved workspaces, then inspect the project structure and read a harmless README or source file. Check that the result matches your real project.

For a read-only workspace, an attempted write should be refused. For AI Review, file modifications should wait for local approval. For AI Auto, compatible allowed changes may apply immediately and appear in history.
bullets: Project tree or file read matches the selected project
The effective write policy matches what the user selected

sections.title: Avoid confusion with command policy
paragraphs: File permissions and command permissions are different. A project may allow reading/writing source files but still require a separate decision for running terminal commands. Inspect both policies when an AI reports a permission refusal.

sections.title: Read the setup panel
paragraphs: Projects detects the selected repository’s framework, package manager, dependency readiness and development command. If preparation is needed, inspect the offered setup before using Prepare project.
Refresh the panel after dependencies or project configuration change. A detected preview address is a runtime observation, so verify that a service is actually listening before opening it.

sections.title: Open files and save durable context
paragraphs: Use the project rail and explorer to select the intended project/file, then use editor or project search for the task. Removing a workspace registration does not delete the project’s contents.
Add a useful project summary, goals and settled decisions in the Project continuity panel so another AI can continue with the right context.

docs.title: Home and local model chat
docs.description: Learn the Home screen: choose a local model, include project context, opt into safe edits and check gateway and remote connection status.

sections.title: What Home provides
paragraphs: Home combines an in-app local model conversation with Gateway, Remote and Quick Actions panels. You can ask a question without an approved project, or select a project to give the chat relevant context.
The model used by Home runs through a supported local runtime. External ChatGPT and other MCP clients connect separately through Connect; your local model selection does not configure those clients.

sections.title: Choose a reachable local model
paragraphs: Start Ollama, LM Studio’s local server or llama.cpp’s server on your machine and make a model available in that runtime. Select a reachable model from Home’s model picker.

RepoTunnel discovers models exposed by the three supported local runtimes and refreshes that discovery while the app is running and when it regains focus. Home’s picker lets you choose among reachable models; it does not silently switch to a cloud model when a runtime is unavailable.
bullets: If Home shows No local model, check that the runtime is running and actually exposes a model.
RepoTunnel discovers models already available through the runtime; it does not automatically install or start that runtime.
Use the selected model’s real capability information when choosing a task.

sections.title: Prepare one runtime before using Home
steps: Choose one supported runtime and install it from its official site. You do not need all three.

In Ollama, download a suitable local model and make sure the local service is running. In LM Studio, download and load a model, open Developer and start the local server. For llama.cpp, follow its server instructions with a compatible local model file.
Return to RepoTunnel’s Home screen and select the reachable model. If it is missing, verify the runtime’s server and loaded model before refreshing RepoTunnel.
sections.note: Check the model’s license, download size and hardware needs before downloading. Home discovers an existing local server; it does not install the runtime or silently replace it with a cloud model.

sections.title: Ask with the right project context
paragraphs: Select the intended project before asking about its code. Home can include bounded project context, the current file, a selected code fragment you explicitly add, and an existing diagnostic you attach.

Use + Selection or + Error when available. Remove a context chip if it does not belong in the next question. Context may be reduced to fit the selected model, and the chat reports that reduction or a context warning.
bullets: Start with a specific question about the selected project.
Check the context sources returned with the response.
Use Shift+Enter for a new line and Enter to send.
Stop generation if the request is no longer useful.

sections.title: Opt into edits for one message
paragraphs: Allow edits is a per-message choice for a selected project. It enables that message to propose safe project edits through RepoTunnel’s editing and History path; the toggle resets after sending.

Keep it off while exploring or asking for an explanation. If you enable it, inspect the resulting change or pending request in History and verify the file contents. Workspace permissions and safe-edit validation still apply.

sections.title: Read the connection panels
paragraphs: Gateway shows whether the local MCP endpoint is online. Remote shows the configured public endpoint or managed client connection and can open Connect.
A running gateway is one layer of the connection. Verify remote work with an authenticated request from the intended AI client against the selected approved project.

sections.title: Use Quick Actions
paragraphs: Open project registers an existing folder; New project starts the app’s project-creation flow. Create checkpoint saves the selected project’s accessible state, and Safety scan checks its protection status.
Pause AI access temporarily blocks MCP workspace access. Resume only when you are ready for those clients to continue. Phone Access has its own local access and pause controls.

links.label: Save a checkpoint before a large change

sections.title: Keep conversations organized
paragraphs: Home stores local conversations and lets you start a new chat, reopen a recent one or delete a conversation from this device. Switching the selected workspace reloads that workspace’s local conversation context.
Deleting a chat and restoring project files are separate operations. Use History when the goal is to recover a file version.

docs.title: Connect ChatGPT
docs.description: Connect ChatGPT to RepoTunnel's authenticated MCP endpoint and verify the connection with a real tool call.

sections.title: Prepare the public connection
paragraphs: Start RepoTunnel, approve one project and complete one provider guide. In Connect, wait for Ready and copy the exact public MCP endpoint displayed by the app, including /mcp.

ChatGPT’s custom-app controls depend on your plan and workspace policy. Check OpenAI’s current developer-mode guide if the controls below are unavailable; a workspace administrator may need to enable access.

links.label: OpenAI’s developer mode and MCP apps guide

sections.title: 1 Open the app settings
steps: Sign in to the ChatGPT account that will use RepoTunnel.
Open Settings → Apps and find the developer-mode controls described in OpenAI’s guide. Enable the feature if your account and workspace permit it.
Start the custom-app creation flow. Use your own private connection for this computer.
sections.note: ChatGPT can change labels and availability. Follow the linked current OpenAI guide when your settings differ.

sections.title: 2 Add RepoTunnel and authorize it
steps: Name the app RepoTunnel and paste the exact public MCP endpoint copied from Connect.
Choose the OAuth authentication path for this endpoint and continue to the authorization prompt.
Confirm the authorization in RepoTunnel’s intended local connection flow. Scan or refresh tools in ChatGPT when prompted.
Finish creating the app, then confirm RepoTunnel is available in the chat’s app selector.
sections.note: A public HTTPS response proves reachability only. OAuth authorization and tool discovery must also succeed.

sections.title: 3 Verify a real project request
paragraphs: Open a new chat, select RepoTunnel and make a read-only request against the one project you approved. Confirm that the response names the intended project and is based on its actual files.
sections.code:
List the approved RepoTunnel workspaces, select my test project,
and read its README. Do not modify any files.

sections.title: Refresh or reconnect when needed
paragraphs: After a RepoTunnel upgrade, use the client’s rescan or refresh flow to load the current tools. Reauthorize if OAuth has expired. A changed provider hostname can require updating or recreating the custom app.
The optional continuation extension helps resume saved exact conversations; it is separate from configuring the MCP app.

docs.title: Install on Linux
docs.description: Use the official Debian, RPM or AppImage release package for x86_64 Linux.

sections.title: Verify the downloaded package
paragraphs: Download the package and checksum file from the same official release. Open a terminal in the folder containing your downloaded package and compute its SHA-256 hash.
Find that exact filename in RepoTunnel-SHA256SUMS.txt and compare the complete hash. Continue with installation only when they match.
sections.note: For the RPM or AppImage, replace the filename with the actual package you downloaded. A mismatch means the file should be downloaded again from the official release.

sections.title: Debian / Ubuntu / Linux Mint
paragraphs: For Linux Mint, Ubuntu and other Debian-family x64 installations, download the official .deb from the v0.4.1 release and open it using the distribution's package installer. Alternatively, use your distribution's package manager on the downloaded local file.
sections.note: Run this from the folder where you downloaded the .deb. Verify the package name and checksum first.

links.label: Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums

sections.title: Fedora / RPM compatible
paragraphs: Use the official .rpm package from the release.

sections.title: AppImage
paragraphs: The AppImage is a portable Linux x64 option. After verifying the downloaded file, mark the AppImage executable and launch it as your normal user. It should not require exposing the MCP gateway to the network.

sections.title: Terminal sandbox requirement
paragraphs: AI terminal/process execution on Linux uses Bubblewrap and is intentionally unavailable if the required sandbox cannot be used. Install Bubblewrap with your distribution package manager if RepoTunnel reports that execution is unavailable.

sections.title: First-run confirmation
paragraphs: Open RepoTunnel, confirm it displays its workspace UI, add one disposable development folder and inspect the status of the local gateway. If the UI opens but AI commands are refused, that may be the intended fail-closed sandbox behavior rather than a broken installation.

docs.title: Install on Windows
docs.description: Install RepoTunnel x64 with the official NSIS .exe or MSI package.

links.label: Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums

sections.title: Security boundary
paragraphs: AI command execution uses an AppContainer + Job Object isolation path on Windows. Native UI Automation support exists, but platform-specific runtime behavior should be validated on Windows before making stronger claims.

sections.title: Verify the download
paragraphs: Download the official installer and RepoTunnel-SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release. Open PowerShell in the download folder and compute the installer’s SHA-256 hash.
Compare the full Hash value with the line for that exact filename in the checksum file. Letter case does not matter; every hexadecimal digit must match before you run the installer.
sections.note: For MSI, replace the filename with RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64_en-US.msi. If the hash differs, download the package again from the official release.

sections.title: First launch and permissions
paragraphs: Run the official x64 installer you downloaded, then open RepoTunnel from the installed application. Add a local project folder and confirm the intended access policy before connecting an AI client.

Windows command isolation uses AppContainer and Job Object boundaries. Workflows that require an AppContainer process to reach an unpackaged local host service via localhost can need additional explicit loopback policy; RepoTunnel does not silently add a system-wide exemption.

sections.title: Platform checks
paragraphs: Check the native feature status before relying on accessibility-driven desktop automation or full managed-process reattachment. Package availability is not evidence that every Linux behavior has been validated on Windows.
If an operation is blocked by sandbox policy, inspect the explicit error and platform guide rather than disabling operating-system security.

docs.title: Install on macOS
docs.description: Choose the Apple Silicon or Intel DMG and understand the current updater safety gate.

links.label: Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums

sections.title: Updater behavior
paragraphs: RepoTunnel supports update discovery on macOS, but in-app update installation is intentionally disabled until replacement/restore safety is verified. Install newer DMGs manually when required.

sections.title: Command isolation
paragraphs: The current macOS AI command backend uses the Seatbelt sandbox-exec compatibility path and fails closed when the required sandbox cannot be used.

sections.title: Install the selected DMG
paragraphs: Before opening the DMG, download the release’s checksum file and compute the package’s SHA-256 in Terminal from the download folder. Compare the full result with the checksum for that exact filename.
Determine whether your Mac uses Apple Silicon or Intel, download the corresponding official DMG, and open the packaged application using normal macOS installation steps.
The current macOS command sandbox uses the Seatbelt sandbox-exec compatibility backend. It may not expose the same native automation behavior as the primary Linux development platform.
sections.note: For an Intel Mac, use RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64.dmg. Continue only when the full hash matches the official checksum file.

sections.title: Updates and recovery
paragraphs: RepoTunnel can discover macOS updates, but in-app update installation is intentionally unavailable while verified replace-and-restore safety is incomplete. Follow official release instructions for manual DMG updates.
Do not override macOS protections or delete RepoTunnel application data just to troubleshoot an update. Preserving approved workspaces, settings and OAuth state is part of the release contract.

docs.title: Connection options
docs.description: Choose between ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Direct HTTPS or the optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel.

sections.title: Raw MCP stays local
paragraphs: The raw MCP gateway binds to loopback. Remote providers forward authenticated traffic to that local service rather than opening the workspace gateway directly to the Internet.

sections.title: Choose a provider
bullets: ngrok: simplest built-in managed path; uses your ngrok account/authtoken
Cloudflare Tunnel: uses your cloudflared runtime, tunnel configuration and hostname
Direct HTTPS: advanced self-routed TLS/ACME path
OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel: optional official tunnel-client path for environments that use it

sections.title: When a connection is actually healthy
paragraphs: A green transport status alone does not prove your AI client can call RepoTunnel. You need the complete path: reachable HTTPS, valid OAuth authorization, MCP tool discovery and a successful tool call against an approved workspace.
The raw local gateway listens on loopback. A public provider exposes only the intended remote surface and must not permit arbitrary local file paths or desktop UI access.

sections.title: Choose based on your situation
paragraphs: Use managed ngrok for a straightforward public HTTPS path when you have an ngrok account. Use Cloudflare Tunnel if you already operate a configured cloudflared tunnel. Use Direct HTTPS when you control the required public hostname, routing and trusted certificate setup.
The optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel is a separate transport for environments with official tunnel-client access. These paths are alternatives; you do not need to enable all of them.

sections.title: Where connection setup lives
paragraphs: Open Connect to inspect the local Gateway, configure the public provider and manage the optional tunnel-client path. The public-provider panel handles configured endpoints and remote authorization lifecycle.

Use HTTPS Setup for the staged advanced Direct HTTPS guidance. When revoking remote access or forgetting a provider, inspect the app’s confirmation and current state; approved local projects are a separate part of the product.

docs.title: Connect with ngrok
docs.description: Create an ngrok account, find your authtoken, connect RepoTunnel’s built-in provider, and verify HTTPS, OAuth and a real workspace call.

sections.title: Before you start
paragraphs: ngrok provides the public HTTPS route from your AI client to RepoTunnel on this computer. RepoTunnel integrates ngrok through its Rust SDK and manages the connection itself. You only need your account’s authtoken for this path.
bullets: RepoTunnel is running and the intended project is approved.
You can sign in to your own ngrok account.
Your computer can reach ngrok over the internet.
Keep RepoTunnel and the computer running while the remote client uses them.

sections.title: 1 Create or sign in to your account
paragraphs: Open the official account page below. Create your account using an available sign-up option and complete the provider’s account verification. If you already have an account, choose Log in.

image.alt: Signed-out ngrok account page with sign-up options and a Log in link
image.caption: ngrok’s public account page, captured 9 October 2026. Complete registration on ngrok; RepoTunnel does not create the account for you.

sections.title: 2 Get your authtoken
paragraphs: Once signed in, open Your Authtoken using the direct link below. Copy the token value into RepoTunnel’s local credential field. If the dashboard presents a command containing the token, copy only the token value, not the command.
The authtoken authorizes RepoTunnel’s ngrok connection. Complete any sign-in prompts on ngrok itself; keep the token out of chats, screenshots and project files.
steps: Sign in to the account whose endpoint and usage limits you want RepoTunnel to use.
Open Your Authtoken and copy your own token.
Keep RepoTunnel’s Connect screen open for the next step.

sections.title: 3 Configure RepoTunnel
paragraphs: The labels below follow the current app source. Installed releases may show slightly different controls.
steps: Open Connect in RepoTunnel and select ngrok in the public-provider selector.
Paste the token into ngrok authtoken.
Choose Set up & connect. If another provider is configured, use the displayed switch action.
Wait until the local gateway is Online and the public connection reports Ready.
Copy the exact MCP HTTPS URL displayed by RepoTunnel. Use its /mcp endpoint in the AI client.

sections.title: 4 Verify the public endpoint
paragraphs: Open the public connection’s health URL using the same hostname as its MCP URL. The hostname and HTTPS response should match RepoTunnel’s running provider. Then finish OAuth in the AI client and perform a real approved-workspace request.
In the following example, replace YOUR-PUBLIC-HOST with the hostname actually shown by RepoTunnel. The health request contains no provider credential.
bullets: The public provider is Ready and the local gateway is Online.
The client completes RepoTunnel OAuth and discovers tools.
A list_workspaces call returns the intended approved project.
A read-only file request works within that project’s access policy.

sections.title: Keep the endpoint working
paragraphs: RepoTunnel stores the configured provider state outside the project and attempts to reuse its assigned endpoint across normal restarts. Keep the exact endpoint displayed by the app as your source of truth; account/domain support and provider limits still apply.
Use Restart connection when the app’s connection needs attention. If the public hostname actually changes, update the AI client’s endpoint and complete authorization again as needed.

sections.title: Troubleshoot the failing stage
paragraphs: Check the displayed provider error before changing configuration. A provider problem, an expired AI-client authorization and a workspace permission refusal have different fixes.
bullets: Token refused: reopen Your Authtoken for the intended account and paste its current value locally.
Provider or account limit: review ngrok usage and the account’s current plan limits.
Gateway Offline: restore the local gateway in RepoTunnel before testing the public route.
Provider Ready but client fails: check the exact MCP URL, OAuth authorization and tool discovery.
Project operation refused: inspect the project’s access mode and protected-path policy.

docs.title: Connect with Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.description: Install cloudflared, create a named Cloudflare Tunnel, route a hostname to RepoTunnel’s local origin, and verify the managed connection.

sections.title: What this setup needs
paragraphs: The built-in Cloudflare provider uses a named tunnel, a tunnel token and a public hostname. RepoTunnel runs the local cloudflared worker and forwards to its reserved loopback origin.
bullets: A Cloudflare account and a domain managed through Cloudflare for the published hostname.
cloudflared installed on the same computer as RepoTunnel.
Permission to create a tunnel and publish its hostname.
RepoTunnel running with an approved project.

sections.title: 1 Install cloudflared
paragraphs: Open Cloudflare’s downloads page, select the correct operating system and CPU architecture, and follow its installation instructions. Install the executable on the computer where RepoTunnel runs.

Return to Connect, select Cloudflare and check for cloudflared detected on this computer. If detection still fails, check the installation location and restart RepoTunnel so it sees the updated environment.

sections.title: 2 Create a named tunnel
paragraphs: In the current Cloudflare dashboard, open Networking, then Tunnels. Create a tunnel with a recognizable name such as repotunnel-desktop. Select the computer’s operating system and architecture under Setup Environment.

The dashboard’s connector instructions include the tunnel credential. Copy the token value from the installation/run command into RepoTunnel’s Cloudflare Tunnel token field. Use RepoTunnel to manage this connection’s worker after installing the executable.
steps: Open the Cloudflare dashboard and select the correct account.
Go to Networking → Tunnels and choose Create Tunnel.
Name the tunnel and create it.
Find the tunnel token in the connector’s Install and Run instructions.
Keep that token in the local app’s credential field; treat it as a secret.

sections.title: 3 Publish the localhost origin
paragraphs: Select the named tunnel, open Routes and choose Add route, then Published application. Pick a subdomain under a domain you administer.

Set Service URL to the HTTP localhost origin reported by RepoTunnel. The current reserved Cloudflare origin is port 43182. This service runs on the same computer as cloudflared; do not use the website preview port, a public hostname, or an arbitrary project development server.

Leave the optional Path field empty to forward all of RepoTunnel’s routes, then save the published route. The HTTP hop here is local to the computer; the client-facing hostname uses HTTPS through Cloudflare.

image.alt: Cloudflare published application dialog with hostname and Service URL fields
image.caption: Cloudflare’s official tutorial shows Routes → Add route → Published application. Its sample service and path are examples; for RepoTunnel use the localhost origin shown in Connect and leave Path empty. Screenshot from the public tutorial at 2:30, © Cloudflare.

sections.title: 4 Connect from RepoTunnel
steps: Open Connect and select Cloudflare.
Paste only the named tunnel’s token into Cloudflare Tunnel token.
Enter the public hostname as an HTTPS origin: https://YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST, replacing YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST with your published hostname. Do not include /mcp in this field.
Choose Set up & connect and wait for the local gateway and public provider to become ready.
Copy RepoTunnel’s displayed MCP endpoint for your AI client.

sections.title: 5 Verify and authorize
paragraphs: Check the named tunnel’s status in Cloudflare and the provider’s readiness in RepoTunnel. Open the hostname’s /health route, then finish RepoTunnel OAuth and request an approved workspace from the intended AI client.
Cloudflare routing and RepoTunnel project permissions are separate boundaries. A successful tunnel does not grant more file, terminal or device access.
sections.note: Replace YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST with the hostname you published in Cloudflare.

sections.title: Use a named tunnel for this provider
paragraphs: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels create temporary trycloudflare.com addresses. They are a testing path and differ from RepoTunnel’s configured named-tunnel flow.

Cloudflare documents changing hostnames, limited concurrent requests and no Server-Sent Events support for Quick Tunnels. Follow the named tunnel and stable hostname setup above for this managed provider.

sections.title: Troubleshoot the failing layer
bullets: cloudflared not detected: verify the executable’s installation and restart the app after environment changes.
Tunnel disconnected: inspect the connector status, tunnel token and outbound network access using Cloudflare’s troubleshooting guide.
Origin unreachable or 502: check the Service URL, same-machine localhost origin and RepoTunnel gateway status.
Unexpected login page: inspect whether an additional Cloudflare Access browser policy is protecting this hostname and whether the MCP client supports it.
Health works but tools fail: verify OAuth discovery, authorization and the exact /mcp endpoint.

docs.title: Direct HTTPS setup for ChatGPT
docs.description: Set up RepoTunnel Direct HTTPS for ChatGPT local projects on Linux, with routing, hostname and TLS checks, screenshots, provider links and troubleshooting.

sections.title: Connect ChatGPT without a monthly tunnel quota
paragraphs: Use Direct HTTPS to connect ChatGPT Web to your approved local projects through your own running RepoTunnel endpoint. RepoTunnel adds no monthly tunnel request quota or connection-credit allowance to this connection.
This guide covers the network setup and verification. Keep RepoTunnel, the public route and the trusted HTTPS endpoint running while you work.

sections.title: Choose the right network path
paragraphs: Direct HTTPS puts TLS on your RepoTunnel computer and requires a reachable public route. The documented Linux Mint path uses Route64 and WireGuard for public IPv6, DuckDNS for the hostname, an IPv4-to-IPv6 frontend when needed, and Let’s Encrypt for a trusted certificate.

If your ISP already provides usable public IPv6, you may be able to use that route instead of Route64. A router behind CGNAT cannot provide normal inbound public IPv4 simply by adding a forwarding rule.
The computer must stay powered on, connected to the internet and running RepoTunnel. Free-service availability and limits are controlled by their providers.

sections.title: 1 Check local requirements
paragraphs: Open HTTPS Setup in RepoTunnel. Its four stages are Local requirements, Internet connection, Choose a hostname and Finish Direct HTTPS. Start with the reported prerequisite checks.

On the documented Linux setup, check WireGuard tools, nftables, OpenSSL, certificate tooling and the system service manager. Use your distribution’s installation instructions for missing components and refresh the screen’s checks.
sections.code:
command -v wg
command -v wg-quick
command -v nft
command -v openssl

sections.title: 2 Create the public IPv6 route
paragraphs: If using the documented Route64 path, open its Manager/Portal, create or sign in to your own account, and create a WireGuard tunnel. Choose an appropriate hub and obtain the generated configuration.

In RepoTunnel’s Internet connection stage, choose Import WireGuard config and use that configuration. The Linux helper can configure the WireGuard service and port redirect rules; inspect the local privileged prompt and the screen’s result.

Keep the generated address prefix, peer values and AllowedIPs as provided. WireGuard private keys belong only in the local configuration. If you configure Linux manually, use an interface name of at most 15 characters, such as rt-direct.

image.alt: Route64 portal sign-in page with its Signup link
image.caption: Route64’s public portal, captured 9 October 2026. The tunnel configuration is obtained inside your own account after signing in.

sections.title: 3 Verify routing and port redirects
paragraphs: Confirm that the tunnel interface is active and has the assigned global IPv6 address. For a manual setup using the example interface name rt-direct, the following commands inspect the service and route.
The documented public mappings are TCP 443 to RepoTunnel’s HTTPS listener on 43183, and TCP 80 to its ACME listener on 43184. The raw MCP origin on 127.0.0.1:43182 stays loopback-only.
sections.code:
systemctl is-active wg-quick@rt-direct
sudo wg show rt-direct
ip -6 addr show dev rt-direct
sudo nft list table inet repotunnel_direct
sections.note: Replace rt-direct with your own configured interface name. These commands inspect the setup; the guided import is the setup action.

sections.title: 4 Create the DuckDNS hostname
paragraphs: Open DuckDNS and sign in using an available provider. Add your own unused subdomain and configure its IPv6/AAAA value to the globally routed IPv6 address from your tunnel or ISP.

Save the DNS configuration. Enter only your hostname, such as your-name.duckdns.org, in RepoTunnel’s Choose a hostname stage and select Verify hostname. The hostname input is not saved until you choose Configure Direct HTTPS.

image.alt: DuckDNS public page with sign-in choices along the top
image.caption: DuckDNS’s signed-out page, captured 9 October 2026. Sign in to create and edit your own subdomain; account tokens are not shown here.

sections.title: 5 Check IPv4 compatibility
paragraphs: Some clients need an IPv4 route even when the computer’s origin is IPv6-only. The documented setup uses Netiter’s IPv4-to-IPv6 frontend alongside the hostname’s existing AAAA record.

Read the frontend’s current instructions and terms, then set the hostname’s A/IPv4 record to the address it currently publishes. Keep the AAAA record pointing to your real IPv6 origin. Re-run Verify hostname and inspect both IPv6 and IPv4 results.
Use the provider’s live address instead of copying a permanently hard-coded IP from an old screenshot. TLS still terminates on your RepoTunnel instance in this documented path.

sections.title: 6 Configure Direct HTTPS
sections.note: A self-signed test certificate confirms local TLS only. It does not establish a trusted remote MCP connection.
steps: Return to HTTPS Setup and confirm the public route and hostname checks have passed.
Choose Configure Direct HTTPS to save the selected hostname and start the local frontend.
Inspect the HTTPS listener, redirect-rule checks and external reachability results.
Copy the app’s endpoint only after the trusted HTTPS checks complete.

sections.title: 7 Obtain a trusted certificate
paragraphs: Once the public hostname resolves correctly and public TCP 80 reaches the ACME challenge listener, use Get trusted certificate in HTTPS Setup. RepoTunnel’s documented hostname setup performs HTTP-01 validation through public port 80 to local port 43184.

Check that TLS certificate becomes Trusted and the HTTPS listener is online. A validation failure needs investigation of DNS, routing, the public port 80 path or the current Certbot error before another attempt.

sections.title: 8 Test health and OAuth discovery
paragraphs: Replace your-name.duckdns.org with your own hostname. A health check should return a trusted HTTPS response from RepoTunnel. Check IPv4 and IPv6 separately when both are expected to work.
The two OAuth metadata responses must reference the same public hostname and MCP resource that your AI client uses. These requests inspect public discovery endpoints and contain no private token.
sections.code:
curl -4 -i https://your-name.duckdns.org/health
curl -6 -i https://your-name.duckdns.org/health
curl -sS https://your-name.duckdns.org/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
curl -sS https://your-name.duckdns.org/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server

sections.title: 9 Connect the AI client
paragraphs: Use the exact HTTPS MCP endpoint displayed by RepoTunnel, complete OAuth, discover tools and perform list_workspaces followed by a permitted project read. A responding /health route alone does not prove the authenticated workspace path.

links.label: Connect ChatGPT and test an action

sections.title: After a reboot or network change
paragraphs: Keep the WireGuard service enabled according to the guided setup. After a reboot or Wi-Fi change, check the tunnel’s status, the app’s gateway/provider state and the public health response before asking the AI client to continue.
A stable hostname can remain the same while the local network changes, provided the public tunnel, DNS route and provider remain valid. The app’s checks are the evidence of recovery.

sections.title: Fix the specific failed check
bullets: No global IPv6: inspect the WireGuard import, service, assigned address and peer handshake.
Missing IPv4 compatibility: follow the frontend instructions and recheck the hostname’s A record.
Certificate validation failure: verify hostname DNS and the public port 80 → 43184 ACME path.
TLS EOF or connection refused: inspect the route, redirects, frontend listener and certificate state.
Host-header 403: inspect the reverse-proxy configuration; keep the loopback gateway’s Host validation enabled.
No actions in the client: confirm OAuth metadata, finish authorization and refresh tool discovery.
