docs.title: Optional Secure MCP Tunnel
docs.description: Understand RepoTunnel’s optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel transport, local setup requirements, key handling and readiness checks.

sections.title: When this transport applies
paragraphs: RepoTunnel retains an optional integration with OpenAI’s tunnel-client for environments that already use Secure MCP Tunnel. It is a separate connection path from the managed public ngrok, Cloudflare and Direct HTTPS providers.
Choose the transport supported by your AI environment. The ordinary public-provider setup does not require this optional tunnel client.

sections.title: Prepare the local connection
paragraphs: Run RepoTunnel’s local gateway and make the supported tunnel-client available on the machine. Supply the tunnel ID and Runtime API key through the local connection controls.
RepoTunnel validates the tunnel ID before starting its managed client. Enter credentials only in the relevant local UI; do not place them in a project, chat transcript or copied example.

sections.title: Understand key handling
paragraphs: The Runtime API key is passed only to the tunnel-client child environment and is not stored by RepoTunnel. It is separate from the provider configuration used by ngrok or Cloudflare.
A reconnect may require entering it again. Missing availability of this optional client should not be interpreted as failure of every supported connection provider.

sections.title: Verify and stop cleanly
paragraphs: Use the client’s health state and then make a real authenticated MCP request against an approved workspace. A launched process alone does not prove that the client can reach the project.
Stopping the local gateway also stops the managed tunnel process. Connection troubleshooting should follow the gateway, transport, authentication and workspace layers in order.

links.label: Verify a connection end to end

docs.title: Workspace access and AI modes
docs.description: Understand the difference between filesystem access and mutation approval policy.

sections.title: Access mode
bullets: Read/write: compatible writes may proceed to the change-policy layer

sections.title: AI Review
paragraphs: Supported mutations are prepared and persisted for local Accept/Reject. Stale-file validation is repeated before an approved change is applied.

sections.title: AI Auto
paragraphs: Compatible mutations can apply immediately, but project boundaries, protected paths, command sandboxing and explicit Git-push permission remain enforced.

sections.title: Read-only always wins
paragraphs: A read-only workspace cannot be modified by AI file tools, regardless of whether the UI currently shows AI Auto or AI Review. The scope of access is the approved workspace, not the entire home folder.
Editing policy determines how a permitted write is finalized: AI Review queues a change for human approval, while AI Auto applies compatible changes and records them in history.

sections.title: Validate with a safe test
paragraphs: Test in a disposable repository: ask for a read, a proposed change and a current change-history lookup. Inspect whether the action was refused, queued or applied according to your chosen policies.
Keep command execution policy separate from file-editing policy. AI Review does not permit remote MCP self-approval of pending actions.

docs.title: Large repositories
docs.description: Use RepoTunnel's paged and resumable read tools for very large projects.

sections.title: Why cursors matter
paragraphs: RepoTunnel ties cursors to relevant source/search state and invalidates them when underlying state changes instead of silently continuing against stale content.

sections.title: A practical exploration sequence
paragraphs: Start with list_workspaces and get_workflow_readiness, then inspect_project_page for a paged file tree. Use fast_search_files to locate relevant terms and read_file_range to fetch only the lines you need.
This reduces repeated full scans and avoids flooding the AI conversation with generated dependencies and unrelated project files.

sections.title: What the index excludes
paragraphs: Broad scanning honors .gitignore/.ignore and skips dependency, cache, build, symbolic-link and known secret paths. The index is for relevance and performance; access.rs remains the actual filesystem security boundary.
An explicit file request is still evaluated against the workspace access guard, even when the index has previously shown that path.

docs.title: Project Memory and live continuity
docs.description: Save a project’s goals, decisions and preferences while using live continuity to recover current work without replaying an entire chat.

sections.title: Open the selected project’s continuity panel
paragraphs: Projects includes a Project continuity panel for the selected workspace. It combines saved human context with a current factual resume snapshot.
The visible state can show In progress, Needs attention or Ready to continue, alongside current Git state, active or last-completed work and the next step.

sections.title: Save the context another AI needs
paragraphs: Choose Add context or Edit context to maintain the project summary, goals, decisions, preferences and next steps. Save the context after making it specific and current.
Describe the desired result and the constraints that should survive a new chat. Keep credentials, tokens and private keys out of project context.
bullets: Goals describe what the project should accomplish.
Decisions record choices that are already settled.
Next steps describe intended follow-up work.

sections.title: Let live facts lead recovery
paragraphs: The live snapshot refreshes from recorded activity, Git and managed runtime state. A saved next step is an intention; a completed operation needs a confirmed result.

After an interruption, ask the AI to inspect the current continuity/resume state, changes, processes and outstanding blockers before continuing. Avoid repeating an operation simply because an older plan says it was next.

sections.title: Use the right recovery tool
paragraphs: Project Memory keeps context; History and checkpoints recover accessible project files. The optional continuation extension can deliver an authorized checkpoint to an exact saved ChatGPT conversation.
These features serve different parts of recovery. Inspect the file state after a restore and the actual runtime state before restarting work.

docs.title: Safe editing and history
docs.description: Use stale-change protection, version history and conservative undo behavior.

sections.title: Stale-change protection
paragraphs: Before applying prepared text changes, RepoTunnel fingerprints the relevant file state. If another editor changes the file before approval, the old change fails rather than overwriting newer content.

sections.title: Undo coverage
bullets: Created directories when safe non-recursive deletion remains possible
Rename/move when the original path is still free
Deleted accessible UTF-8 files when restoration is safe

sections.title: Conservative failures
paragraphs: When RepoTunnel cannot confirm a safe rollback or history finalization, it reports failure/ambiguity and retains recovery evidence instead of claiming success.

sections.title: A normal edit lifecycle
paragraphs: In AI Review, the model prepares a bounded mutation and RepoTunnel persists a diff/pending action. The human inspects and accepts or rejects it in the desktop UI; the remote MCP client cannot approve its own request.
In AI Auto, a compatible write is applied without an additional local confirmation and is recorded with history and recovery state when possible.
bullets: Revalidate the live file state before finalization
Apply or queue according to policy
Inspect history and verify final content

sections.title: What Undo does not promise
paragraphs: Text edits have conservative recovery rules. RepoTunnel will not overwrite newer content when an earlier edit is undone. Binary deletion and recursive directory removal may be auditable without having a safe automatic undo point.
Always check the specific history record before assuming a destructive operation can be reversed.

docs.title: History and saved versions
docs.description: Use History to review pending AI edits, inspect activity, search saved versions and restore an earlier accessible project state safely.

sections.title: Select the project first
paragraphs: The activity and saved-version timeline follows the selected approved project. Choose the intended project in the Projects rail, then inspect its recorded work and local file versions.

Pending AI Review changes can span approved projects. Check each request’s workspace name and paths before applying or rejecting it. The Checkpoints manager can also switch between Active project only and All projects; a pending request has not changed the project yet.

sections.title: Review a pending request
paragraphs: In AI Review, inspect the request’s workspace label, paths and prepared diff before choosing the local approval or rejection control. RepoTunnel revalidates the live file before applying a prepared text change; another editor’s intervening changes can make that request stale.
AI Auto applies compatible changes immediately and records their outcome. Read-only access still blocks writes, and an AI cannot approve its own pending request through MCP.

sections.title: Find the activity you need
paragraphs: Search history by the visible record text, select an activity filter and choose newest or oldest first. Load More reveals additional records when the first page is insufficient.

The filters include Files, Terminal, Processes, Apps, Browser, Git, Verification, Monitoring and Team. Expand a record to inspect its recorded outcome instead of treating a request or started process as a completed task.

sections.title: Understand versions and request grouping
paragraphs: File-changing requests can have a local restore point. When a client supplies a usable request trace, RepoTunnel can group the related mutations into one version. Without that trace, changes remain protected but can be stored as separate versions.
Terminal, browser and other activity can appear alongside the file version. Restoring files does not promise to reverse every external side effect recorded in that activity.

sections.title: Return to a saved file state
paragraphs: Select Restore this version on the intended saved entry and review the local confirmation. Previous and Next navigate saved version state; Restore original targets the state captured before the first AI edit.
Later saved versions remain available after a version restore, so you can return to them. Check the returned result, inspect the project and run the appropriate verification before resuming edits.

sections.title: Undo and restore have different scope
paragraphs: Undo reverses a supported individual change only while the relevant current contents and paths still allow safe recovery. Version restore targets a saved project-file state.

Some destructive operations remain auditable without automatic Undo, including recursive removal or deletion that could not be backed up safely as bounded text. Inspect the specific record’s available recovery controls.

sections.title: Manage retention deliberately
paragraphs: Clear All History removes saved versions and activity for that project after local confirmation. Current project files stay as they are, and pending AI Review requests remain available.
Use Settings for the configured version-history and checkpoint retention limits. Clearing saved recovery data removes recovery options; it is a separate decision from accepting an edit.

docs.title: Create and restore checkpoints
docs.description: Save a project checkpoint before a large change, compare it with current files, and understand restoration and retention boundaries.

sections.title: What a checkpoint captures
paragraphs: A checkpoint records the project state that RepoTunnel’s AI access layer can safely read. Protected secrets and ignored build/dependency folders are outside that accessible snapshot.

Use checkpoints as local recovery points for a selected approved project. They complement Git commits and ordinary file-edit versions; they do not capture the entire machine or every external service.

sections.title: Create one before a large change
paragraphs: Choose the correct project, open Home and select Create checkpoint. Wait for RepoTunnel’s saved result, then open History to find the new checkpoint.
Give a useful checkpoint a recognizable name. The manager supports renaming and pinning records so an important recovery point is easier to identify.
bullets: Confirm the selected project before creating the snapshot.
Use a name that describes the working state you intend to preserve.
Check that the saved record appears before starting the larger task.

sections.title: Compare before restoring
paragraphs: In History’s Checkpoints section, select the record and inspect its comparison with the current project. The comparison reports modified files, files added since the checkpoint and files now missing.
Search, date grouping and Load More help locate an older checkpoint. Use All projects or Active project only to choose the visible scope, and review the affected paths before approving a restore.

sections.title: Restore and verify the result
paragraphs: Restoration requires read/write access to the checkpoint’s project. It returns the AI-accessible files to the captured state, including removing new accessible files created after the checkpoint. Protected and ignored files remain outside that restoration.

Select the intended checkpoint, review the affected paths and read the local confirmation. RepoTunnel creates a fresh pre-restore checkpoint first. Inspect the returned restored/removed-file result and run relevant verification before resuming work; running services and remote actions are separate state.

sections.title: Delete only the recovery data you intend
paragraphs: Deleting one checkpoint removes that recovery point without changing current project files. Clear All Checkpoints uses the manager’s current scope: all approved projects in All projects view or when no project is selected, otherwise the active project.

The local confirmation identifies that scope, and clearing includes pinned checkpoints. Check it before confirming. Retention is configured in Settings; protected-file rules remain in force during capture, comparison and restoration.

docs.title: Verification commands vs live terminal
docs.description: Choose the correct execution surface for testing or real project processes.

sections.title: Choose a project in Commands
paragraphs: Commands combines the selected project’s live terminal, managed processes, application launcher, browser controls and monitoring. Confirm the project and execution surface before running work.

The app exposes command policy separately from file access and AI-change policy. Read-only access and native sandbox requirements still matter; inspect a denial rather than attempting an unrestricted fallback.

sections.title: Run disposable verification
paragraphs: Use a discovered build/test/check/lint preset when a temporary copy is sufficient. This path disables networking, bounds execution/output and discards incidental writes after the command.

Supported discovery includes safe-named package scripts, Cargo checks/tests/builds, Python test discovery and Go tests/builds. Arbitrary shell strings, deployment/publish commands and development servers are not disposable presets.

sections.title: Run a live one-shot command
paragraphs: Use Live terminal for a finite command in the real approved project when the work needs persistent changes or permitted network access. Choose a workspace-relative working directory if the command belongs below the root.
Inspect status, duration, exit code and captured output. A nonzero exit or a queued approval is not a successful command result.

sections.title: Start and manage a long-running process
paragraphs: Use a managed process for development servers, watchers and background workers. Follow its running/exited/stopped state and incremental logs, then stop or restart the specific process when appropriate.

Managed identity/history survives normal MCP/UI reconnects. Full app-restart reattachment is currently advertised on Linux; Windows/macOS remain unavailable until equivalent native recovery is validated.

sections.title: Approve through the local controls
paragraphs: The disposable command policy can be review, automatic or disabled. Pending command definitions are rechecked before local approval so a changed script cannot silently replace the one you reviewed.

In AI Auto, supported live commands/process starts can execute immediately. In AI Review they follow the applicable command policy and may wait for local Accept/Reject. MCP cannot approve its own pending request.

sections.title: Inspect the application and recorded evidence
paragraphs: Use the launcher and managed browser controls for UI verification when the task needs them, then correlate output and monitoring state. Confirm a local preview responds rather than assuming a started server is ready.
Pause AI is the emergency boundary for active AI live execution and managed process groups. Keep the result tied to the exact project and runtime you inspected.

docs.title: Checks and project readiness
docs.description: Understand the Checks screen, Ready/Limited/Blocked results, and the next step for a project before AI edits, verification or Git work.

sections.title: Run a read-only readiness check
paragraphs: Open Checks, choose the approved project and select Check workflow. You can run this local inspection before connecting ChatGPT.
The check inspects whether the project can support the development sequence. It does not create test files, execute project code, stage files or make a commit.

sections.title: Read the result
bullets: Ready: the project’s inspection, safe editing, sandbox verification and Git workflow capabilities are available.
Limited: inspection works, while one or more later steps need setup or are intentionally unavailable.
Blocked: RepoTunnel cannot safely validate the approved workspace.

sections.title: Follow the recommended next step
paragraphs: Read each reported item and the Recommended next step rather than relying only on the overall badge. A read-only project, disabled commands, unavailable native sandbox, missing discovered preset or unsupported Git layout can limit the workflow.
Fix the specific setup or permission issue locally and select Run again. Keep read-only access when the requested work is inspection; a Limited result can accurately describe that intentional choice.

sections.title: Verify the remote path separately
paragraphs: Checks shows whether the gateway/client path is connected alongside project readiness. A successful local check does not establish that a remote AI client has authenticated and can call the tools.
Use Connect to configure the transport, then verify a real workspace-list or bounded-read request from the client.

links.label: Set up and verify a connection

sections.title: Move through the development loop
paragraphs: Once the required capabilities are ready, inspect the project, prepare the intended change, run an appropriate verification command and inspect Git state.
Use Commands for actual build/test/check execution. Return to History for recorded results and file recovery, and to Git when you are ready to review or stage the intended changes.

docs.title: Git workflow
docs.description: Inspect, stage and commit through RepoTunnel's fixed Git capability surface.

sections.title: Mutation safeguards
bullets: Hooks/GPG signing disabled for controlled commit execution

sections.title: Push
paragraphs: Push remains separate from normal in-project autonomy and requires a current explicit human instruction.

sections.title: Inspect before publishing
paragraphs: Use RepoTunnel's bounded Git status/diff/log tools. Staging accepts specific project-relative paths, rechecks the live file/index state and blocks protected/secret-bearing content. Committing operates on the exact staged snapshot, not an arbitrary shell command.
Use safe restore-to-HEAD only for eligible files and remember that it still passes the normal history/review boundary.

sections.title: Publishing is a separate decision
paragraphs: AI Auto permits compatible local edits and commits, but it does not mean the user permanently authorized pushing code. A push must represent the current user's explicit publishing intent and passes a final secret preflight.
Avoid broad force/mirror/delete/all/tags pushes through RepoTunnel's controlled flow. If the user has not requested publication, stop at a locally verified commit.

sections.title: Know which repository layouts are supported
paragraphs: The approved workspace root must contain its own .git directory. Parent-repository and linked-worktree layouts are rejected because their metadata can live outside the approved root.
Restore-to-HEAD is limited to eligible unstaged, non-conflicted tracked text files and uses the safe-editing path. Staged changes are not silently discarded.

sections.title: Inspect GitHub connection state
paragraphs: RepoTunnel can broker supported authenticated GitHub work without exposing its credential to the AI shell. A sandboxed command not seeing a token is not proof that GitHub is disconnected.
Keep account/security changes local and check the app’s authoritative connection status.

docs.title: Managed browser
docs.description: Run browser verification inside RepoTunnel's managed Chromium-family runtime.

sections.title: Document-aware state
paragraphs: Navigation returns document-generation information so observations can be tied to the intended page rather than an older document.

sections.title: Start with isolated browser state
paragraphs: RepoTunnel uses a managed Chromium-family browser runtime rather than assuming that a human’s ordinary browser tab is available to AI. Its browser profiles and tab/session state are controlled by RepoTunnel.
Use browser inspection for current DOM, screenshots for visual context, and diagnostics for console/network errors. Navigation receipts bind the observed page to the new document state.
bullets: Open a target URL in an owned tab
Inspect the page before clicking or typing
Verify the result and check diagnostics when needed

sections.title: Downloads and uploads
paragraphs: Browser uploads may select only an existing file within an approved workspace. Configured downloads are routed into RepoTunnel-owned temporary workspaces, then intentionally kept outputs may be moved into the selected project.
Do not treat a downloaded filename as proof that the file finished successfully; inspect the reported download status.

docs.title: Semantic browser actions
docs.description: Use short-lived accessibility references and mutation receipts instead of stale element assumptions.

sections.title: Short-lived refs
paragraphs: Semantic element references are bound to the current snapshot/session and are revalidated before a mutation.

sections.title: Ambiguous mutations
paragraphs: If transport is lost after a click/type may have been dispatched, RepoTunnel records an ambiguous outcome and observes current state instead of replaying the action.

sections.title: Find and act on the live page
paragraphs: Short-lived semantic element references are tied to the browser session and document state. After a navigation, significant DOM change or failed action, inspect the page again and obtain a new reference instead of reusing an old one.
Sensitive input fields are protected. A failure to type a password or payment credential through the semantic path is intentional.

sections.title: How to handle uncertain outcomes
paragraphs: A network or helper failure after dispatch may mean a click or type action already changed the remote site. RepoTunnel records a mutation receipt and returns an ambiguous status rather than replaying it.
Before repeating a state-changing action, inspect the current page URL, document generation, form values and any resulting confirmation. Retry only when you have evidence that it did not happen.
sections.note: Never interpret ambiguous as failed. An automatic second click could place a duplicate order or submit a form twice.

docs.title: AI Workspace
docs.description: Run supported GUI apps in RepoTunnel's isolated virtual desktop.

sections.title: Use AI Workspace when
paragraphs: The AI needs a GUI application but should not interrupt or take over your ordinary desktop session.

sections.title: Choose the right control surface
paragraphs: AI Workspace uses an isolated desktop for AI-owned application sessions, so the human can continue working in their normal session. Normal Desktop Control is different: it targets permitted applications already running on the human desktop.
For browser-driven tasks, use RepoTunnel managed browser automation rather than starting a new Chrome process inside AI Workspace.

sections.title: A reliable GUI workflow
paragraphs: Start or reattach to one allowed app session and inspect its windows. Observe the selected window before acting; use a semantic accessibility reference when possible, with window-relative coordinates as a grounded fallback.
After important mutations, verify the actual application state. Losing a chat session does not imply the GUI app should be closed or restarted.
bullets: Keep a stable appSessionId for ownership
Avoid password/credential input through protected automation paths

sections.title: Native platform boundaries
paragraphs: Linux isolates accessibility through a private AT-SPI environment. Windows UI Automation and macOS Accessibility adapters exist, but native behavior must be verified on those operating systems before making platform-specific claims.

docs.title: Phone Access
docs.description: Connect a selected Android device with explicit capability controls.

sections.title: Access modes
bullets: Pause AI as a separate emergency control

sections.title: Transport
paragraphs: Wireless Debugging is preferred. Authorized USB can act as fallback for the same selected device.

sections.title: Capabilities
bullets: Semantic helper actions and bounded transactions

sections.title: Prepare the selected Android device
paragraphs: Phone Access works only with a phone selected locally by the human. Wireless Debugging is preferred when authorized, with USB fallback for the same device when supported. The AI receives an opaque target device identity, not a raw adb serial.
The bundled Phone Helper provides bounded semantic accessibility actions, but the user must grant Android Accessibility permission on the phone itself. RepoTunnel does not silently turn it on.

sections.title: Pair and confirm the device locally
steps: On the Android phone, enable Developer options. For supported Android 11+ Wi-Fi pairing, put the computer and phone on the same network and open Wireless debugging.
Use RepoTunnel’s local Phone pairing controls with the phone’s current pairing details. Pairing details belong in that local flow rather than an AI chat.
Select the intended paired phone in RepoTunnel, choose Limited or Full locally and grant only the capabilities you need.
If the Phone Helper requests Android Accessibility permission, grant it on the phone yourself. Verify the live screen belongs to the selected device before asking the AI to act.
sections.note: Menu names vary by phone vendor. USB fallback still requires the phone’s local debugging authorization. Pairing and permission changes remain under your control.

image.alt: Android Wireless debugging settings showing the switch and Pair device with pairing code
image.caption: Google’s official Android example shows Wireless debugging and Pair device with pairing code. Device menus can differ by vendor. © Google, CC BY 4.0.

sections.title: Use the least access needed
paragraphs: Off blocks AI Phone access; Limited permits individually enabled capabilities; Full exposes the supported set subject to the phone’s own OS and app policy. Pause AI is an independent emergency boundary.
MCP cannot pair/select a new device, raise capability grants or unpause Phone Access. These controls remain local to the user.
bullets: View the live screen when permitted
Use bounded app/file/settings tools only when enabled
Re-check the foreground application before sensitive actions

sections.title: Understand OS denial
paragraphs: An Android vendor, profile policy or application may refuse an operation even when Phone Access says Full. That is an OS-level result, not proof that RepoTunnel failed. Inspect the reported error before trying an alternative.

docs.title: Phone privacy and sensitive apps
docs.description: Understand the non-bypass behavior around payment-sensitive Android applications.

sections.title: Foreground protection
paragraphs: When a payment-sensitive application is foreground, RepoTunnel blocks AI screen observation, semantic access, raw input, generic shell and relevant diagnostic paths. It does not attempt to bypass the app's security model.

sections.title: User remains authoritative
paragraphs: MCP cannot pair/select a phone, grant itself more Phone capabilities or unpause access. Android permissions and device policy remain authoritative.

sections.title: Why payment-sensitive apps are special
paragraphs: When a payment-sensitive app is foreground, RepoTunnel blocks AI screen observation, raw input, semantic actions and related bypass paths. The user can leave that app to resume eligible automation.
Full Access does not bypass financial-app security boundaries, passwords, OTPs, system permission prompts or device policies.

sections.title: Good verification practice
paragraphs: Test input and observation against a non-financial app only. To verify the block, check that RepoTunnel reports access denied without attempting real balances, payments or credential entry.
The bundled helper may remain enabled while observation is blocked; an enabled helper does not imply authorization to read a sensitive screen.

docs.title: Team Mode workflow
docs.description: Coordinate two AI engineers with enforced ownership and review boundaries.

sections.title: Create a Team from GPT Agents
paragraphs: Open GPT Agents in the desktop sidebar and select the approved project. Enter the product goal and one concrete success criterion per line, then create the Team.

Copy the separate Engineer A and Engineer B kickoff prompts into the two intended AI chats. They join once and keep their identities until you choose End Team. Keep the project’s access and change policy appropriate for their task.

sections.title: Planning
bullets: Each creates a distinct initial implementation task

sections.title: Review and completion
bullets: Findings return to the task owner
Success criteria are verified with evidence
Complete closes the current request, not the persistent Team

sections.title: Split the work before editing
paragraphs: A persistent A/B Team does not mean two agents should race through one task. Both engineers join, post plans, create distinct initial implementation tasks, and confirm the split. Only then is parallel implementation unlocked.
Each agent owns at most one active implementation task and must hold task scoped path claims for its edits. Shared browser interaction is serialized through an exclusive resource claim.

sections.title: Cross-review and evidence
paragraphs: Each engineer implements a meaningful scope. The other engineer reviews it and gives concrete feedback when a defect requires correction. Success criteria are verified with actual test/build/browser evidence.
Completing a request closes only that request’s work cycle; the persistent team remains attached until the human chooses to end it.

sections.title: Avoid duplicate work
paragraphs: If a task owner is blocked, use a deliberate handoff rather than letting the second agent independently implement the same files. Refresh team status and wait for the other engineer to post their work instead of guessing what they changed.

sections.title: Read the desktop progress view
paragraphs: The app shows the current work request, workflow stage, engineer status, task owners/reviewers, verified success criteria and recommended action. It intentionally hides the raw live coordination feed from the main Team screen.

Completing the request returns the persistent Team to Ready. Pause is temporary; End Team ends the collaboration. An attached AI can register the next human request into the same Team without new kickoffs.

docs.title: Continuity / Resume v2
docs.description: Resume from current Git, activity and process state instead of stale saved notes.

sections.title: Factual state wins
paragraphs: RepoTunnel's resume snapshot prioritizes current Git/process/activity evidence and treats Project Memory as semantic context rather than unquestioned live state.

sections.title: Use after interruption
paragraphs: After an MCP reconnect, app restart or chat interruption, inspect the resume snapshot first and continue from the persisted live state rather than restarting already-completed work.

sections.title: Recover facts before intentions
paragraphs: Resume v2 considers live Git status, recent activity, managed processes and bounded project context. Saved Project Memory captures useful user decisions, not an authoritative claim that an older task is still open.

After a reconnect or interrupted session, inspect the live resume snapshot first. Compare its recent completed operations with current working-tree state before deciding whether any mutation needs repeating.

sections.title: What recovery does not do
paragraphs: RepoTunnel cannot detect every way an external chat generation can end, and it should not claim to restart arbitrary conversations invisibly. Its continuation features depend on explicitly supported runtime and client integration.
It is safer to report unresolved/ambiguous work than to claim completion from an old memory or duplicate a side-effectful command.

sections.title: Use the app’s Project continuity panel
paragraphs: In Projects, inspect the selected workspace’s Current state, active or last-completed work and next step. Add or edit human context when goals or decisions change; factual progress continues updating from activity.
Use History for saved file state and the optional extension only for eligible exact-chat delivery.

docs.title: ChatGPT continuation extension
docs.description: Install the optional Chromium continuation extension, save exact ChatGPT chats, understand its status and privacy, and troubleshoot safe delivery.

sections.title: What the companion does
paragraphs: RepoTunnel Continuation delivers a RepoTunnel-authorized continuation checkpoint to an exact ChatGPT conversation you explicitly save. It helps the supported continuation workflow resume in that chat after a safely completed turn.

It is optional. The desktop MCP gateway, project permissions and ordinary AI work do not require the extension. Keep factual Project Memory and Resume v2 state current even when you use the companion.

sections.title: Get the source folder
paragraphs: The extension lives at extensions/chatgpt-continuation in the RepoTunnel repository’s main branch. Obtain that source folder before using Load unpacked; select the extension folder containing manifest.json rather than the repository root.
The already-published v0.4.1 desktop release does not list a separate extension asset. This guide does not imply a browser-store listing or an extension installer bundled into that desktop package.

sections.title: Install in a compatible Chromium browser
paragraphs: The project documents Chrome/Chromium 102 or newer, or a compatible Chromium-based browser. RepoTunnel must be running locally.
sections.note: Keep the unpacked installation in a stable folder after pairing. Do not delete RepoTunnel application data to change an extension installation.
steps: Open the browser’s extensions page, such as chrome://extensions in Chrome/Chromium or edge://extensions in Edge.
Enable Developer mode.
Choose Load unpacked and select extensions/chatgpt-continuation.
Open your exact https://chatgpt.com/c/... conversation.
Open RepoTunnel Continuation from the browser toolbar.
Choose Add current ChatGPT chat.

image.alt: Official Chrome example showing Developer mode and Load unpacked on the extensions page
image.caption: Google’s official example highlights Developer mode and Load unpacked. Select RepoTunnel’s extensions/chatgpt-continuation folder for your installation; the sample extension pictured is Google’s tutorial example. © Google, CC BY 4.0.

sections.title: Save the exact conversations you want
paragraphs: You can save up to five exact conversations. A general ChatGPT home URL is not a target, and the companion does not guess another conversation when a saved one is unavailable.
Keep the intended saved chat open. Duplicate tabs for the same conversation are refused by the documented continuation flow; close the unnecessary duplicate and inspect status before retrying.

sections.title: Read the extension status
bullets: Not set: no ChatGPT conversation is saved.
Waiting: a saved conversation has not recently registered with the local RepoTunnel bridge.
Connected: the saved conversation has recently registered with RepoTunnel.
sections.note: Connected confirms recent registration. It does not mean there is a checkpoint to send or that a delivery has completed.

sections.title: Understand safe delivery
paragraphs: The extension waits for an idle completed assistant response and an empty composer. It protects recent human typing, prepares the checkpoint, obtains authorization from RepoTunnel, attempts one send and seeks a positive acknowledgement.
If a crash or transport failure makes the post-send outcome uncertain, the message is not automatically replayed. Inspect the actual chat and continuation state before deciding how to recover.

sections.title: Know the data and permissions
paragraphs: The extension stores exact saved conversation URLs, tab titles and bounded connection/delivery status in extension-local storage, with temporary bridge-health state in session storage.

Its declared hosts are chatgpt.com and the dedicated local bridge at 127.0.0.1:43185. It requests activeTab, alarms, scripting and storage for the saved-chat and heartbeat workflow. The documented companion has no analytics, advertising, telemetry or third-party tracking.

sections.title: Troubleshoot a waiting checkpoint
paragraphs: Check that RepoTunnel is running, the intended chat is saved and open at its exact conversation URL, the turn is idle, and the composer is empty. Recent typing, a duplicate tab, an active response or unavailable bridge can keep delivery waiting.

RepoTunnel pins the first valid extension origin that registers. Preserve a working paired installation until you intentionally migrate it; replacing folders or clearing app data is not a routine waiting-state fix.

docs.title: Video Intelligence
docs.description: Analyze supported media with bounded background jobs.

sections.title: Open Video and choose Analyze
paragraphs: Video’s Analyze view is for understanding supported public media or approved local project media. Its displayed modes are Full, Transcript focus, Visual focus and Tutorial focus.

Select the intended media/project and mode, add a time range when useful, start analysis and follow the cancellable job’s progress. Fetch or inspect the final content only after the result is available.

sections.title: Evidence handling
paragraphs: RepoTunnel checks existing captions first, extracts bounded smart frames when visuals matter, and prepares compact audio only when captions are unavailable and speech understanding is needed.

sections.title: No execution authority
paragraphs: Instructions discovered inside media do not authorize installs, edits, browser actions or other local mutations.

sections.title: Select the analysis mode
paragraphs: Transcript mode is appropriate when speech is the primary question. Visual mode focuses on frames and design, instruction mode on tutorial steps, and full mode combines speech and visuals.

Analysis uses bounded background jobs and may rely on existing captions, selected frames and compact audio processing when needed. The result should distinguish what was actually observed from inferred interpretation.

sections.title: Use analysis results safely
paragraphs: Instructions spoken in a video are not authorization to install software, delete files, change browser state or publish code. Follow-up actions still pass the normal RepoTunnel policies.
Media helpers such as yt-dlp and ffmpeg may need provisioning under protected application data when absent; supported provisioners verify trusted downloads rather than silently changing system PATH.

docs.title: Video Production
docs.description: Maintain durable Video Projects with script, scenes, narration, subtitles, rendering and QA.

sections.title: Open Video and choose Projects
paragraphs: Use Video’s Projects view for production work and keep the intended durable Video Project selected. Analyze is the neighboring evidence-gathering view for existing media.
Treat a script, storyboard, scene generation, draft render and QA result as separate pipeline states. Check the project’s current status before repeating a stage after an interruption.

sections.title: Pipeline
paragraphs: The canonical production pipeline is Script → Storyboard → Voice → Scenes → Assembly → QA → Export.

sections.title: Resource policy
paragraphs: New Video Projects default to no automatic large model/runtime downloads and paid services blocked. Managed model downloads require explicit policy plus per-request opt-in.

sections.title: Create a durable Video Project
paragraphs: Video Production maintains project-owned script, storyboard, scene, timeline, narration, assets, previews, render jobs, QA and license records. This allows interrupted production work to resume without confusing an output file with completed QA.
The tutorial/explainer path prefers lightweight deterministic HTML/CSS/GSAP scene capture where its dependencies exist, with a native 2D fallback. Story mode has separate director and render routing.

sections.title: Verify before final export
paragraphs: Plan the spec, script and storyboard, choose a suitable rendering method and resources, then build the scenes. Generate a low-resolution design preview, inspect representative frames and fix design issues before final rendering.
Check the final media with ffprobe and the Video Project QA report. A successful FFmpeg exit is not, by itself, proof that output resolution, timing, audio and subtitles are correct.

sections.title: Resource and provenance safety
paragraphs: RepoTunnel does not require large local AI models or paid providers as a condition of basic production. Resource policies gate automatic installation/downloads; external assets must keep their license and source records.

docs.title: Security model
docs.description: Understand RepoTunnel's layered local security boundaries.

sections.title: Default position
paragraphs: Access is denied unless a project or capability has been explicitly enabled through RepoTunnel's user-controlled surfaces.

sections.title: Do not bypass host policies
paragraphs: RepoTunnel is designed to work with operating-system, browser, Android, application and external-service security policies rather than bypass them.

sections.title: Where the trust boundary lives
paragraphs: The Rust backend mediates registered workspace IDs, protected filesystem paths, safe editing and command execution. The raw MCP gateway stays bound to loopback and public HTTPS paths are subject to authenticated transport and OAuth rules.
AI Auto removes repeated approval prompts only for compatible authorized operations. It is not unrestricted host access or permanent permission to publish Git history.

sections.title: Separate capability grants
paragraphs: Desktop, Phone, browser, Git, AI Workspace and terminal operations have different guards. Permission for one does not silently enable another. User-controlled Phone escalation and desktop self-control restrictions cannot be bypassed through a different MCP action.

sections.title: Know the limitations
paragraphs: This model applies to RepoTunnel-controlled paths. Applications a person runs manually outside RepoTunnel are not sandboxed by RepoTunnel. macOS uses its current Seatbelt compatibility backend, with a long-term stronger native replacement still a platform consideration.

docs.title: Secrets and protected paths
docs.description: Understand the files and outputs RepoTunnel intentionally protects.

sections.title: Output handling
paragraphs: RepoTunnel redacts credential-like terminal/process output and does not intentionally log project source, API keys or raw credentials.

sections.title: Never put credentials in project docs
paragraphs: Do not commit OAuth refresh tokens, private keys, ngrok/Cloudflare tokens or tunnel secrets into projects or website source. Provider credentials belong in the supported local configuration paths.

Protected-path filters, output redaction, Git secret scanning and restricted child-process environments each provide separate defenses; they do not make it safe to paste credentials into a public issue.

sections.title: Check publish boundaries
paragraphs: RepoTunnel validates staged Git content and performs a final secret check before an explicitly authorized push. External Git clean filters and local hooks are restricted along controlled mutation paths.
If a suspected secret was ever published, revoke/rotate the credential at the provider. Simply removing a token from the latest commit may not remove it from remote history.

docs.title: Platform status
docs.description: Know which RepoTunnel behaviors are packaged versus natively validated.

sections.title: Linux
paragraphs: Primary live-validated development platform. Linux supports managed-process reattachment after a full RepoTunnel restart.

sections.title: Windows
paragraphs: Packages are produced for x64. Command isolation uses AppContainer + Job Object. Native UI Automation adapters exist and require native compatibility validation for specific runtime claims.

sections.title: macOS
paragraphs: Apple Silicon and Intel DMGs are produced. The current command sandbox uses Seatbelt compatibility. Update discovery is supported while in-app update installation remains intentionally disabled pending verified recovery safety.

sections.title: What “supported” means
paragraphs: Release packages exist for Linux x64, Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Intel. Package compatibility, native automation acceptance and long-running process recovery are separate questions.
Linux is the primary verified development target. Windows uses AppContainer + Job Object for sandboxed commands; macOS uses the current Seatbelt compatibility backend.

sections.title: Check feature-specific limits
paragraphs: Complete RepoTunnel process restart reattachment for managed jobs is currently Linux-only. Native desktop accessibility behavior requires native testing on Windows/macOS, and macOS in-app update installation is intentionally disabled pending recovery validation.
Consult the current release notes and platform documentation before advertising full native feature parity.

docs.title: MCP capability reference
docs.description: Understand the shape of RepoTunnel's capability-oriented MCP surface without relying on a hard-coded tool count.

sections.title: Compatibility rule
paragraphs: Clients may cache MCP schemas. Refresh or rescan RepoTunnel actions after a schema change before assuming a new tool is missing.

sections.title: Tool discovery and compatibility
paragraphs: Use the MCP client’s discovery/rescan flow to fetch the current RepoTunnel tool schema. Avoid hard-coding a total tool count; features evolve and some clients cache action definitions.

Workspace tools accept approved workspace IDs and relative paths rather than arbitrary host paths. Several mutation operations are not equivalent to simple filesystem calls because they can queue approval or enforce secret checks.

sections.title: Read before mutation
paragraphs: Start with workspace discovery and readiness, inspect relevant files and policy, then perform the smallest authorized action. For long commands, use managed processes and inspect their output.
After edits, verify actual source content or Git diff. After browser mutations, inspect the page again when the receipt is ambiguous. After Phone operations, respect the current capability state.

docs.title: Settings, updates and Help
docs.description: Find runtime diagnostics, signed update controls, startup and history-retention settings, plus built-in guidance and keyboard shortcuts.

sections.title: Inspect the installation in Settings
paragraphs: Open Settings for Runtime diagnostics. Review the installed version, platform/architecture and availability of required tools before diagnosing an unavailable feature.

Refresh the diagnostics after changing the local setup. A missing optional tunnel client matters only if you use that transport; native sandbox availability matters when the task needs AI command execution.

sections.title: Manage signed updates
paragraphs: Check for updates queries the official release channel. Automatic checks controls periodic discovery; an available release can show its notes and the Update & Restart action.

Save pending editor work and inspect the displayed installation-block reason before updating. macOS currently supports update discovery while in-app installation is disabled pending verified replacement/restore safety.

sections.title: Choose startup behavior
paragraphs: Settings can enable or disable Launch at login. Starting the application and establishing a usable AI connection are separate states; inspect Gateway and Remote after startup.
The optional Secure MCP Tunnel Runtime API key is not persisted by RepoTunnel. Configured public providers have their own lifecycle and recovery behavior.

sections.title: Set history and checkpoint retention
paragraphs: Review the configured limits for saved versions and checkpoints in Settings. These controls govern retained local recovery records rather than the files in your project.
History and Checkpoints also provide explicit clear/delete actions. Review those confirmations carefully when you still need an older recovery point.

sections.title: Use Help for built-in guidance
paragraphs: Help explains approved projects, AI Auto/AI Review, the local security boundary, Git publishing and recovery. Its shortcut groups cover the workspace, editor and terminal.
Use the shortcut labels shown by your current app/platform. The source Help panel lists the following common actions.
bullets: Ctrl+P: Quick Open; Ctrl+Shift+P: Command Palette; Ctrl+Shift+F: Search Project.
Ctrl+S: save; Ctrl+F: find in file; Ctrl+G: go to line.
Ctrl+Shift+T: reopen a closed tab; Ctrl+Shift+Enter: Focus Mode.
Terminal Enter: run a command; Ctrl+Enter: start a managed process.
Terminal Ctrl+F: search output; Ctrl+L: clear displayed terminal content.

docs.title: Connection troubleshooting
docs.description: Diagnose a RepoTunnel connection without weakening the local security boundary.

sections.title: Public connection is not Ready
bullets: Restart the configured connection from RepoTunnel
Confirm the public health endpoint where applicable
Run a real authenticated MCP tool call after transport health is restored

sections.title: ChatGPT asks to reconnect
paragraphs: Use ChatGPT's reconnect/reauthorize flow and approve the RepoTunnel authorization request. A normal reconnect should not require deleting your approved project state.

sections.title: Tools look stale
paragraphs: Refresh or rescan the RepoTunnel app/actions in the MCP client if RepoTunnel's MCP schema changed.

sections.title: Diagnose each layer separately
paragraphs: First establish that RepoTunnel itself is running and has an approved workspace. Next inspect gateway/provider readiness, the exact public HTTPS endpoint, and OAuth authorization. Finally verify MCP tool discovery and a real workspace call.
If a public /health endpoint responds but tool discovery fails, inspect OAuth/DCR/PKCE and client configuration rather than assuming a working end-to-end connection.

sections.title: Avoid an unsafe quick fix
paragraphs: Never bind the raw MCP gateway to a public interface or disable Host validation to work around a connection problem. Direct HTTPS reverse proxy configuration must adapt forwarded Host headers without weakening the local loopback guard.

sections.title: After upgrading RepoTunnel
paragraphs: A client can keep an older cached MCP schema. Refresh or rescan actions after upgrading or switching the connector and then retest with list_workspaces. A missing action does not automatically mean the server failed to start.

docs.title: Terminal troubleshooting
docs.description: Understand why RepoTunnel may intentionally refuse AI command execution.

sections.title: Linux
paragraphs: If Bubblewrap is missing or unusable, RepoTunnel blocks AI terminal execution rather than falling back to an unrestricted shell. Install/fix Bubblewrap and restart RepoTunnel.

sections.title: Credential access
paragraphs: A sandboxed shell not seeing a GitHub token does not mean RepoTunnel's trusted GitHub connection is disconnected. The trusted GitHub broker intentionally keeps credentials out of the AI shell.

sections.title: Distinguish policy denial from a crash
paragraphs: An unavailable native sandbox is an intentional fail-closed refusal. RepoTunnel does not run AI commands on the unrestricted host simply because Bubblewrap, Windows AppContainer or the macOS backend cannot be initialized.
Read the exact error, inspect configured command policy and compare host-vs-sandbox tool visibility using environment diagnostics.

sections.title: Understand hidden credentials
paragraphs: Sandboxed AI terminal sessions intentionally omit many credential files and sensitive environment variables. A trusted RepoTunnel GitHub connection can support allowlisted GitHub operations without giving the AI shell direct access to the credential.
Do not work around missing credentials by copying your token into the workspace or exporting it in terminal output.
